## Loading → Success (`status-button`)

The button morphs into a spinner, then a green checkmark or a red shake.

- API: `StatusButton("…", status:) { }`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/StatusButton.swift

### Usage

```swift
@State private var status = MotionButtonStatus.idle

StatusButton("Pay now", status: status) {
    status = .loading
    Task {
        status = await pay() ? .success : .failure
        try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.5))
        status = .idle
    }
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI StatusButton (iOS 17+) driven by a status enum: idle, loading, success, failure. It is a 50 pt tall capsule Button. Idle shows the title at its natural width. For any other status the frame width animates to 50 pt, turning the capsule into a circle (spring response 0.45, damping 0.75), and the title shrinks and fades. Loading shows a white 70% arc spinning forever. Success turns the fill green and draws a white checkmark path with trim from 0 to 1 (easeOut 0.35 s, 0.15 s delay). Failure turns the fill red, scales in an xmark and shakes horizontally with a GeometryEffect (8 pt, three swings). Play success and error haptics with sensoryFeedback, disable the button when not idle, and expose the status as the accessibility value.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// The phases a `StatusButton` moves through.
public enum MotionButtonStatus: Equatable, Sendable {
    case idle
    case loading
    case success
    case failure
}

/// A capsule button that morphs to show the result of its action: it shrinks
/// into a spinning circle while loading, then turns green with a drawn
/// checkmark on success, or red with a shake on failure.
///
/// You own the status, so it works with any async work:
///
/// ```swift
/// @State private var status = MotionButtonStatus.idle
///
/// StatusButton("Pay now", status: status) {
///     status = .loading
///     Task {
///         status = await pay() ? .success : .failure
///         try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.5))
///         status = .idle
///     }
/// }
/// ```
public struct StatusButton: View {
    private let title: LocalizedStringKey
    private let status: MotionButtonStatus
    private let tint: Color
    private let action: () -> Void

    @State private var spin = false
    @State private var shakes = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let height: CGFloat = 50

    public init(
        _ title: LocalizedStringKey,
        status: MotionButtonStatus,
        tint: Color = .accentColor,
        action: @escaping () -> Void
    ) {
        self.title = title
        self.status = status
        self.tint = tint
        self.action = action
    }

    public var body: some View {
        Button(action: action) {
            ZStack {
                Text(title)
                    .font(.headline)
                    .lineLimit(1)
                    .fixedSize()
                    .padding(.horizontal, 28)
                    .opacity(status == .idle ? 1 : 0)
                    .scaleEffect(status == .idle ? 1 : 0.6)

                if status == .loading {
                    Circle()
                        .trim(from: 0, to: 0.7)
                        .stroke(.white, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 3, lineCap: .round))
                        .frame(width: 22, height: 22)
                        .rotationEffect(.degrees(spin ? 360 : 0))
                        .onAppear {
                            spin = false
                            withAnimation(.linear(duration: 0.8).repeatForever(autoreverses: false)) {
                                spin = true
                            }
                        }
                        .transition(.scale(scale: 0.4).combined(with: .opacity))
                }

                CheckmarkShape()
                    .trim(from: 0, to: status == .success ? 1 : 0)
                    .stroke(.white, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 3.5, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
                    .frame(width: 20, height: 16)
                    .animation(status == .success ? .easeOut(duration: 0.35).delay(0.15) : nil, value: status)

                Image(systemName: "xmark")
                    .font(.system(size: 18, weight: .bold))
                    .scaleEffect(status == .failure ? 1 : 0.3)
                    .opacity(status == .failure ? 1 : 0)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .frame(width: status == .idle ? nil : height, height: height)
            .background(Capsule().fill(background))
            .contentShape(Capsule())
        }
        .buttonStyle(StatusPressStyle())
        .disabled(status != .idle)
        .modifier(StatusShake(shakes: CGFloat(shakes)))
        .animation(.spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.75), value: status)
        .onChange(of: status) { _, newValue in
            if newValue == .failure, !reduceMotion {
                withAnimation(.linear(duration: 0.4)) { shakes += 1 }
            }
        }
        .haptic(trigger: status) { _, newValue in
            switch newValue {
            case .success: .success
            case .failure: .error
            default: nil
            }
        }
        .accessibilityLabel(Text(title))
        .accessibilityValue(accessibilityStatus)
    }

    private var background: Color {
        switch status {
        case .idle, .loading: tint
        case .success: .green
        case .failure: .red
        }
    }

    private var accessibilityStatus: Text {
        switch status {
        case .idle: Text("")
        case .loading: Text("Loading")
        case .success: Text("Done")
        case .failure: Text("Failed")
        }
    }
}

private struct StatusPressStyle: ButtonStyle {
    func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
        configuration.label
            .scaleEffect(configuration.isPressed ? 0.95 : 1)
            .animation(.spring(response: 0.25, dampingFraction: 0.6), value: configuration.isPressed)
    }
}

/// Horizontal shake, one full shake per unit of `shakes`.
private struct StatusShake: GeometryEffect {
    var shakes: CGFloat

    var animatableData: CGFloat {
        get { shakes }
        set { shakes = newValue }
    }

    func effectValue(size: CGSize) -> ProjectionTransform {
        ProjectionTransform(CGAffineTransform(translationX: 8 * sin(shakes * .pi * 6), y: 0))
    }
}

/// A checkmark drawn left to right, sized to its frame.
struct CheckmarkShape: Shape {
    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: rect.midY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX + rect.width * 0.38, y: rect.maxY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.minY))
        return path
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var status = MotionButtonStatus.idle

        var body: some View {
            StatusButton("Pay now", status: status) {
                status = .loading
                DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 1.2) { status = .success }
                DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 2.8) { status = .idle }
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Glow Border (`glow-border`)

A rainbow border runs around the view with a soft glow behind it.

- API: `.glowBorder()`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/GlowBorder.swift

### Usage

```swift
Text("Upgrade to Pro")
    .padding()
    .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14))
    .glowBorder(cornerRadius: 14)

CardView()
    .glowBorder(colors: [.orange, .yellow], cornerRadius: 24, lineWidth: 3)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .glowBorder(colors:cornerRadius:lineWidth:glowRadius:duration:) view modifier (iOS 17+). In a non-interactive overlay, use TimelineView(.animation) to compute a rotation angle of (time / duration) turns (3 s per turn). Build an AngularGradient from the palette plus its first colour again (pink, purple, blue, cyan, mint by default) starting at that angle. Stroke a continuous RoundedRectangle with it twice: once at 2× line width, blurred by glowRadius (8) at 80% opacity for the glow, and once crisp at lineWidth (2). With Reduce Motion on, pause the rotation.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A gradient border that keeps rotating around the view, with a soft glow
/// behind it. Draws attention to a primary action or a highlighted card.
struct GlowBorderModifier: ViewModifier {
    var colors: [Color]
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat
    var lineWidth: CGFloat
    var glowRadius: CGFloat
    var duration: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
                    let turns = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate / duration
                    let gradient = AngularGradient(
                        colors: colors + [colors.first ?? .clear],
                        center: .center,
                        angle: .degrees(turns.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1) * 360)
                    )
                    let shape = RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous)
                    ZStack {
                        shape.stroke(gradient, lineWidth: lineWidth * 2)
                            .blur(radius: glowRadius)
                            .opacity(0.8)
                        shape.stroke(gradient, lineWidth: lineWidth)
                    }
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Adds a rotating gradient border with a glow.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Text("Upgrade to Pro")
    ///     .padding()
    ///     .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14))
    ///     .glowBorder(cornerRadius: 14)
    /// ```
    func glowBorder(
        colors: [Color] = [.pink, .purple, .blue, .cyan, .mint],
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 14,
        lineWidth: CGFloat = 2,
        glowRadius: CGFloat = 8,
        duration: Double = 3
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(GlowBorderModifier(
            colors: colors,
            cornerRadius: cornerRadius,
            lineWidth: lineWidth,
            glowRadius: glowRadius,
            duration: duration
        ))
    }
}

#Preview {
    Text("Upgrade to Pro")
        .font(.headline)
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .padding(.horizontal, 28)
        .padding(.vertical, 16)
        .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14, style: .continuous))
        .glowBorder()
        .padding(40)
}
```

## Shine (`shine`)

A slanted glint of light sweeps across the button, on cue or on a beat.

- API: `.shine(every:) / .shine(trigger:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Value change / Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Shine.swift

### Usage

```swift
PremiumBadge()
    .shine(every: 3)

Button("Upgrade") { purchases += 1 }
    .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    .shine(trigger: purchases)
```

### How it works

Create two SwiftUI modifiers (iOS 17+): .shine(trigger:color:duration:) and .shine(every:color:duration:). Both overlay a "band": a horizontal LinearGradient clear → white 70 % → clear, 30 % of the view's width (at least 24 pt), twice the view's height, rotated 20°, whose x offset goes from −1.5 × band (fully off the left) at progress 0 to width + 1.5 × band (off the right) at progress 1. Mask the band with the content so only the view's own pixels shine, and disable hit testing. The trigger version runs progress 0 → 1 with keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 0, trigger:) and one CubicKeyframe over duration (0.75 s), so the band is hidden at rest. The looping version uses TimelineView(.animation) with progress = (time mod interval) / duration, clamped to 1. With Reduce Motion on, skip the band.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A slanted glint of light that sweeps across the view once, either every
/// time `trigger` changes or on a fixed interval.
struct ShineModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Trigger
    var color: Color
    var duration: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Reduce Motion: no sweep.
        let enabled = !reduceMotion
        let color = color
        return content
            .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 0.0, trigger: trigger) { view, progress in
                view.overlay {
                    if enabled {
                        ShineBand(progress: progress, color: color).mask { view }
                    }
                }
            } keyframes: { _ in
                // 0 and 1 are both off the view, so the band is hidden at rest.
                CubicKeyframe(1, duration: duration)
            }
    }
}

/// Repeats the glint every `interval` seconds.
struct LoopingShineModifier: ViewModifier {
    var interval: Double
    var color: Color
    var duration: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.overlay {
            if !reduceMotion {
                TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
                    let time = timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
                    let phase = time.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: max(interval, duration))
                    ShineBand(progress: min(1, phase / duration), color: color)
                }
                .mask { content }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The band itself: a skewed white gradient that travels left to right as
/// `progress` goes from 0 to 1.
private struct ShineBand: View {
    var progress: Double
    var color: Color

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let width = geometry.size.width
            let band = max(24, width * 0.3)
            LinearGradient(colors: [.clear, color, .clear], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing)
                .frame(width: band, height: geometry.size.height * 2)
                .rotationEffect(.degrees(20))
                .offset(x: -band * 1.5 + (width + band * 3) * progress, y: -geometry.size.height / 2)
        }
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Sweeps a glint of light across the view every time `trigger` changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Button("Upgrade") { purchases += 1 }
    ///     .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    ///     .shine(trigger: purchases)
    /// ```
    func shine<Trigger: Equatable>(
        trigger: Trigger,
        color: Color = .white.opacity(0.7),
        duration: Double = 0.75
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ShineModifier(trigger: trigger, color: color, duration: duration))
    }

    /// Sweeps a glint of light across the view every `interval` seconds.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// PremiumBadge()
    ///     .shine(every: 3)
    /// ```
    func shine(
        every interval: Double,
        color: Color = .white.opacity(0.7),
        duration: Double = 0.75
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(LoopingShineModifier(interval: interval, color: color, duration: duration))
    }
}

#Preview {
    Text("Go Premium")
        .font(.headline)
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .padding(.horizontal, 24)
        .padding(.vertical, 12)
        .background(Capsule().fill(Color.orange.gradient))
        .shine(every: 2)
        .padding()
}
```

## Jelly (`jelly`)

A rubbery squash-and-stretch wobble on every tap.

- API: `.jelly(trigger:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Jelly.swift

### Usage

```swift
Button("Boing") { taps += 1 }
    .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    .jelly(trigger: taps)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .jelly(trigger:amount:) view modifier (iOS 17+) using keyframeAnimator(initialValue:trigger:) on a struct with x and y scale (both 1), applied with scaleEffect(x:y:). With a = amount (0.25): the x track goes 1 + a (0.1 s), 1 − 0.8a (0.12 s), 1 + 0.5a (0.12 s) with cubic keyframes, then a SpringKeyframe(.bouncy) back to 1 over 0.4 s; the y track does the opposite (1 − a, 1 + 0.8a, 1 − 0.5a, spring to 1), so the view squashes wide and flat, then stretches tall and thin, then settles. With Reduce Motion on, use a = 0.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

private struct JellyScale {
    var x: CGFloat = 1
    var y: CGFloat = 1
}

/// A rubbery squash-and-stretch wobble that plays every time `trigger`
/// changes: wide and flat, then tall and thin, settling back with a spring.
struct JellyModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Trigger
    var amount: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Reduce Motion: stay still.
        let a = reduceMotion ? 0 : amount
        return content.keyframeAnimator(initialValue: JellyScale(), trigger: trigger) { view, scale in
            view.scaleEffect(x: scale.x, y: scale.y)
        } keyframes: { _ in
            KeyframeTrack(\.x) {
                CubicKeyframe(1 + a, duration: 0.1)
                CubicKeyframe(1 - a * 0.8, duration: 0.12)
                CubicKeyframe(1 + a * 0.5, duration: 0.12)
                SpringKeyframe(1, duration: 0.4, spring: .bouncy)
            }
            KeyframeTrack(\.y) {
                CubicKeyframe(1 - a, duration: 0.1)
                CubicKeyframe(1 + a * 0.8, duration: 0.12)
                CubicKeyframe(1 - a * 0.5, duration: 0.12)
                SpringKeyframe(1, duration: 0.4, spring: .bouncy)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Wobbles the view like jelly every time `trigger` changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Button("Boing") { taps += 1 }
    ///     .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    ///     .jelly(trigger: taps)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameter amount: How far it squashes (0.25 = 25 %).
    func jelly<Trigger: Equatable>(trigger: Trigger, amount: CGFloat = 0.25) -> some View {
        modifier(JellyModifier(trigger: trigger, amount: amount))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var taps = 0
        var body: some View {
            Button("Boing") { taps += 1 }
                .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                .controlSize(.large)
                .jelly(trigger: taps)
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding(40)
}
```

## Click Spark (`click-spark`)

Short spark lines shoot out from the exact point you tapped.

- API: `.clickSpark()`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/ClickSpark.swift

### Usage

```swift
Button("Launch") { }
    .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    .clickSpark(color: .orange)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .clickSpark(color:count:radius:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Detect taps with .simultaneousGesture(SpatialTapGesture()) and append a spark (UUID + location) to a @State array, removing it 0.6 s later. In a hit-testing-disabled overlay, place each spark at its location: count (8) capsules 2.5 pt wide and 0.45 × radius tall, each rotated by index / count × 360°. On appear, animate with easeOut(0.45 s) from offset −0.3 × radius to −radius (outward), scaleEffect(y:) from 1 to 0.1 anchored at the top (so each line shrinks toward its outer tip) and opacity from 1 to 0. With Reduce Motion on, don't add sparks.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Short spark lines shoot out from the exact point the user tapped.
struct ClickSparkModifier: ViewModifier {
    var color: Color
    var count: Int
    var radius: CGFloat

    @State private var sparks: [Spark] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private struct Spark: Identifiable {
        let id = UUID()
        let location: CGPoint
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                ZStack {
                    ForEach(sparks) { spark in
                        SparkLines(color: color, count: count, radius: radius)
                            .position(spark.location)
                    }
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .simultaneousGesture(
                SpatialTapGesture().onEnded { value in
                    // Reduce Motion: no sparks.
                    guard !reduceMotion else { return }
                    let spark = Spark(location: value.location)
                    sparks.append(spark)
                    DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.6) {
                        sparks.removeAll { $0.id == spark.id }
                    }
                }
            )
    }
}

private struct SparkLines: View {
    let color: Color
    let count: Int
    let radius: CGFloat

    @State private var fired = false

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            ForEach(0..<max(1, count), id: \.self) { index in
                Capsule()
                    .fill(color)
                    .frame(width: 2.5, height: radius * 0.45)
                    // Shrinks toward its outer end as it flies.
                    .scaleEffect(y: fired ? 0.1 : 1, anchor: .top)
                    .offset(y: -(fired ? radius : radius * 0.3))
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(Double(index) / Double(max(1, count)) * 360))
            }
        }
        .opacity(fired ? 0 : 1)
        .onAppear {
            withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.45)) { fired = true }
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Shoots spark lines out of every tap point.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Button("Launch") { }
    ///     .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    ///     .clickSpark(color: .orange)
    /// ```
    func clickSpark(color: Color = .orange, count: Int = 8, radius: CGFloat = 28) -> some View {
        modifier(ClickSparkModifier(color: color, count: count, radius: radius))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16)
        .fill(.black)
        .frame(width: 260, height: 160)
        .overlay(Text("Click anywhere").foregroundStyle(.white))
        .clickSpark()
}
```

## Like Button (`like-button`)

The heart pops in as a ring bursts open and coloured dots fly out.

- API: `LikeButton(isLiked:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/LikeButton.swift

### Usage

```swift
LikeButton(isLiked: $post.isLiked)

LikeButton(isLiked: $liked, size: 40, color: .red)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI LikeButton (iOS 17+) bound to isLiked, with size (28 pt), color (pink) and dotColors. It's a plain Button showing Image(systemName: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart"); tapping toggles and, on like, increments a counter used as a keyframeAnimator trigger over a struct {heart, ring, dots}. Tracks: heart drops to 0.2 instantly, holds 0.15 s, then springs to 1 with a bouncy overshoot; ring goes 0 → 1 over 0.3 s then back to 0; dots wait 0.15 s then go 0 → 1 over 0.55 s. Behind the heart draw (a) a circle strokeBorder in color whose diameter is 1.5 × size × ring and whose line width is 0.5 × size × (1 − ring), so it bursts open and thins out; (b) 7 pairs of small dots (0.16 × size) at angles i/7 × 360° ± 10°, at distance size × (0.6 + 0.55 × dots), scaling down to 10 % as they fly. Unliking only springs the heart back. Add a light haptic on like, and hide the burst for Reduce Motion.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

private struct LikePop {
    var heart: CGFloat = 1
    var ring: CGFloat = 0
    var dots: CGFloat = 0
}

/// A Twitter-style like button: on like, a ring bursts open, the heart pops
/// in with an overshoot and a circle of coloured dots flies out. Unliking
/// just shrinks the heart back.
public struct LikeButton: View {
    @Binding private var isLiked: Bool
    private let size: CGFloat
    private let color: Color
    private let dotColors: [Color]

    @State private var likes = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isLiked: Whether the item is liked; tapping toggles it.
    ///   - size: Point size of the heart.
    ///   - color: Colour of the filled heart and the ring.
    ///   - dotColors: Colours cycled through by the burst dots.
    public init(
        isLiked: Binding<Bool>,
        size: CGFloat = 28,
        color: Color = .pink,
        dotColors: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .yellow, .mint, .cyan, .purple]
    ) {
        _isLiked = isLiked
        self.size = size
        self.color = color
        self.dotColors = dotColors
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let showBurst = !reduceMotion
        let size = size, color = color, dotColors = dotColors
        return Button {
            isLiked.toggle()
            if isLiked { likes += 1 }
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
                .font(.system(size: size))
                .foregroundStyle(isLiked ? color : Color.secondary)
                .frame(width: size * 1.6, height: size * 1.6)
                .contentShape(Rectangle())
                .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: LikePop(), trigger: likes) { heart, pop in
                    heart
                        .scaleEffect(pop.heart)
                        .background {
                            if showBurst { LikeBurst(pop: pop, size: size, color: color, dotColors: dotColors) }
                        }
                } keyframes: { _ in
                    KeyframeTrack(\.heart) {
                        CubicKeyframe(0.2, duration: 0.05)
                        CubicKeyframe(0.2, duration: 0.15)
                        SpringKeyframe(1, duration: 0.5, spring: .bouncy(duration: 0.4, extraBounce: 0.25))
                    }
                    KeyframeTrack(\.ring) {
                        LinearKeyframe(0.01, duration: 0.01)
                        CubicKeyframe(1, duration: 0.3)
                        LinearKeyframe(0, duration: 0.01)
                    }
                    KeyframeTrack(\.dots) {
                        LinearKeyframe(0, duration: 0.15)
                        CubicKeyframe(1, duration: 0.55)
                        LinearKeyframe(0, duration: 0.01)
                    }
                }
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .animation(.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.6), value: isLiked)
        .haptic(.lightImpact, trigger: likes)
        .accessibilityLabel(isLiked ? "Unlike" : "Like")
    }
}

/// The ring and the dots behind the heart.
private struct LikeBurst: View {
    let pop: LikePop
    let size: CGFloat
    let color: Color
    let dotColors: [Color]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            // The ring grows and its stroke thins out to nothing.
            if pop.ring > 0 {
                Circle()
                    .strokeBorder(color, lineWidth: max(0.1, size * 0.5 * (1 - pop.ring)))
                    .frame(width: size * 1.5 * pop.ring, height: size * 1.5 * pop.ring)
            }
            // Seven pairs of dots fly outward and shrink.
            if pop.dots > 0 {
                ForEach(0..<14, id: \.self) { index in
                    dot(index)
                }
            }
        }
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func dot(_ index: Int) -> some View {
        let pair = index % 2
        let base = Double(index / 2) / 7 * 2 * .pi - .pi / 2
        let angle = base + (pair == 0 ? -0.18 : 0.18)
        let reach: CGFloat = 0.6 + 0.55 * pop.dots
        let distance: CGFloat = size * reach * (pair == 0 ? 1 : 0.85)
        let fill: Color = dotColors.isEmpty ? color : dotColors[index % dotColors.count]
        return Circle()
            .fill(fill)
            .frame(width: size * 0.16, height: size * 0.16)
            .scaleEffect(1 - pop.dots * 0.9)
            .offset(x: CGFloat(cos(angle)) * distance, y: CGFloat(sin(angle)) * distance)
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var liked = false
        var body: some View {
            LikeButton(isLiked: $liked, size: 40)
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding(60)
}
```

## Animated Symbol (`animated-symbol`)

SF Symbols that keep moving: bounce on a beat, pulse, variable colour.

- API: `AnimatedSymbol("…", style:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/AnimatedSymbol.swift

### Usage

```swift
AnimatedSymbol("bell.fill")                      // bounces every 1.5 s
AnimatedSymbol("heart.fill", style: .pulse)
AnimatedSymbol("wifi", style: .variableColor)
AnimatedSymbol("mic.fill", style: .scaleUp, isActive: isRecording)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI AnimatedSymbol view (iOS 17+) wrapping Image(systemName:) with a style enum: .bounce, .pulse, .variableColor and .scaleUp, plus isActive and interval (1.5 s). For .bounce, apply .symbolEffect(.bounce, value: beats) and increment beats in a .task(id: isActive) loop every interval. For the others, use the indefinite effects .symbolEffect(.pulse, isActive:), .symbolEffect(.variableColor.iterative.reversing, isActive:) and .symbolEffect(.scale.up, isActive:). The view inherits font and foregroundStyle like any Image. With Reduce Motion on, treat it as inactive.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// An SF Symbol that keeps playing a symbol effect: a bounce on a beat, or a
/// continuous pulse, variable-colour cycle or scale-up.
public struct AnimatedSymbol: View {
    /// Which symbol effect to play.
    public enum Style: CaseIterable, Sendable {
        /// Bounces once every `interval` seconds.
        case bounce
        /// Fades the symbol's layers in and out.
        case pulse
        /// Lights up the symbol's layers one after another (wifi, speaker…).
        case variableColor
        /// Grows the symbol slightly and holds it.
        case scaleUp
    }

    private let systemName: String
    private let style: Style
    private let isActive: Bool
    private let interval: Double

    @State private var beats = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - systemName: The SF Symbol name.
    ///   - style: The effect to play.
    ///   - isActive: Pauses the effect when false.
    ///   - interval: Seconds between bounces (`.bounce` only).
    public init(_ systemName: String, style: Style = .bounce, isActive: Bool = true, interval: Double = 1.5) {
        self.systemName = systemName
        self.style = style
        self.isActive = isActive
        self.interval = interval
    }

    public var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: the symbol stays still.
        let active = isActive && !reduceMotion
        let image = Image(systemName: systemName)
        Group {
            switch style {
            case .bounce:
                image.symbolEffect(.bounce, value: beats)
            case .pulse:
                image.symbolEffect(.pulse, isActive: active)
            case .variableColor:
                image.symbolEffect(.variableColor.iterative.reversing, isActive: active)
            case .scaleUp:
                image.symbolEffect(.scale.up, isActive: active)
            }
        }
        .task(id: active) {
            guard style == .bounce, active else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                beats += 1
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(max(0.3, interval)))
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    HStack(spacing: 24) {
        AnimatedSymbol("bell.fill")
        AnimatedSymbol("heart.fill", style: .pulse)
        AnimatedSymbol("wifi", style: .variableColor)
        AnimatedSymbol("mic.fill", style: .scaleUp)
    }
    .font(.largeTitle)
    .padding()
}
```

## Liquid Toggle (`liquid-toggle`)

A switch whose knob stretches like a drop of liquid as it slides.

- API: `.toggleStyle(.liquid)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/LiquidToggleStyle.swift

### Usage

```swift
Toggle("Wi-Fi", isOn: $wifi)
    .toggleStyle(.liquid)

Toggle("Dark mode", isOn: $dark)
    .toggleStyle(.liquid(tint: .purple))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI LiquidToggleStyle (iOS 17+) with a tint (green) and static accessors .liquid and .liquid(tint:). makeBody puts the label, a Spacer and a 52 × 32 pt switch in an HStack. The switch is a plain Button that toggles configuration.isOn inside withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.7)); it shows a ZStack aligned .trailing when on and .leading when off, with a capsule track (tint when on, gray 35 % when off) and a white capsule knob (26 pt tall, 3 pt padding, small shadow). The knob's width runs a keyframeAnimator triggered by isOn: CubicKeyframe to 1.5 × 26 pt over 0.12 s, then SpringKeyframe(.bouncy) back to 26 over 0.35 s, so it stretches as it slides and snaps back round. Give it an "On"/"Off" accessibility value. With Reduce Motion on, don't stretch and use a short ease.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A switch whose knob stretches like a drop of liquid as it slides across,
/// then springs back to a circle.
///
/// ```swift
/// Toggle("Wi-Fi", isOn: $isOn)
///     .toggleStyle(.liquid)
///
/// Toggle("Dark mode", isOn: $dark)
///     .toggleStyle(.liquid(tint: .purple))
/// ```
public struct LiquidToggleStyle: ToggleStyle {
    public var tint: Color

    public init(tint: Color = .green) {
        self.tint = tint
    }

    public func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
        HStack {
            configuration.label
            Spacer(minLength: 12)
            LiquidSwitch(isOn: configuration.$isOn, tint: tint)
        }
    }
}

private struct LiquidSwitch: View {
    @Binding var isOn: Bool
    let tint: Color

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let width: CGFloat = 52
    private let height: CGFloat = 32
    private let knob: CGFloat = 26

    var body: some View {
        let knob = knob
        // Reduce Motion: no stretch.
        let stretch = reduceMotion ? knob : knob * 1.5
        return Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.7)) {
                isOn.toggle()
            }
        } label: {
            ZStack(alignment: isOn ? .trailing : .leading) {
                Capsule()
                    .fill(isOn ? tint : Color.gray.opacity(0.35))
                Capsule()
                    .fill(.white)
                    .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.2), radius: 2, y: 1)
                    .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: knob, trigger: isOn) { view, knobWidth in
                        view.frame(width: knobWidth, height: knob)
                    } keyframes: { _ in
                        CubicKeyframe(stretch, duration: 0.12)
                        SpringKeyframe(knob, duration: 0.35, spring: .bouncy)
                    }
                    .padding(3)
            }
            .frame(width: width, height: height)
            .contentShape(Capsule())
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityValue(isOn ? "On" : "Off")
    }
}

public extension ToggleStyle where Self == LiquidToggleStyle {
    /// A switch with a stretchy, liquid knob.
    static var liquid: LiquidToggleStyle { LiquidToggleStyle() }

    /// A switch with a stretchy, liquid knob in the given colour.
    static func liquid(tint: Color) -> LiquidToggleStyle { LiquidToggleStyle(tint: tint) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var on = true
        var body: some View {
            Toggle("Notifications", isOn: $on)
                .toggleStyle(.liquid)
                .frame(width: 240)
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}
```

## Staggered Entrance (`staggered-appear`)

List items fade and rise into place one after another.

- API: `.staggeredAppear(index:)`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/StaggeredAppear.swift

### Usage

```swift
ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
    CardView(item)
        .staggeredAppear(index: index)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .staggeredAppear(index:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for list and grid entrances. Each item starts at opacity 0, offset 24 pt down and scale 0.96, then on appear animates to its resting state with .spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.8), delayed by index × 0.08 s so the items cascade in. Delay per item and travel distance are configurable.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Items fade, rise and settle into place one after another when they first
/// appear.
struct StaggeredAppearModifier: ViewModifier {
    var index: Int
    var delayPerItem: Double
    var distance: CGFloat

    @State private var visible = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .opacity(visible ? 1 : 0)
            // Reduce Motion: fade only.
            .offset(y: visible || reduceMotion ? 0 : distance)
            .scaleEffect(visible || reduceMotion ? 1 : 0.96)
            .onAppear {
                withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.8).delay(Double(index) * delayPerItem)) {
                    visible = true
                }
            }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Staggered entrance. Give each item in a list its position.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
    ///     CardView(item)
    ///         .staggeredAppear(index: index)
    /// }
    /// ```
    func staggeredAppear(index: Int, delayPerItem: Double = 0.08, distance: CGFloat = 24) -> some View {
        modifier(StaggeredAppearModifier(index: index, delayPerItem: delayPerItem, distance: distance))
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(spacing: 12) {
        ForEach(0..<5, id: \.self) { index in
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
                .fill(Color.accentColor.opacity(0.2 + Double(index) * 0.15))
                .frame(height: 56)
                .staggeredAppear(index: index)
        }
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## 3D Tilt (`tilt`)

Card tilts in 3D toward the finger with a moving glare, then springs flat.

- API: `.tiltOnDrag()`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/Tilt.swift

### Usage

```swift
CardView()
    .tiltOnDrag(maxAngle: 15, cornerRadius: 20)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .tiltOnDrag() view modifier (iOS 17+). While the user drags on the view, convert the drag translation into a normalised -1…1 value per axis (120 pt = full tilt) and apply two rotation3DEffects (x axis from vertical drag, y axis from horizontal drag) up to a max angle of ~12°, plus a 1.03 scale. Overlay a white glare gradient whose start/end points follow the tilt and which is only visible while dragging, clipped to the card's corner radius. Use .interactiveSpring while dragging and a bouncy spring back to flat on release.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// 3D card tilt that follows the finger, with a moving glare, then springs
/// back flat on release.
struct TiltModifier: ViewModifier {
    var maxAngle: Double
    var glare: Bool
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat

    /// Normalised drag, each axis in -1...1.
    @State private var tilt: CGSize = .zero
    @State private var isDragging = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// Translation (in points) that maps to the maximum angle.
    private let range: CGFloat = 120

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                if glare {
                    LinearGradient(
                        colors: [.white.opacity(isDragging ? 0.35 : 0), .clear],
                        startPoint: UnitPoint(x: 0.5 - tilt.width * 0.5, y: 0.5 - tilt.height * 0.5),
                        endPoint: UnitPoint(x: 0.5 + tilt.width * 0.5, y: 0.5 + tilt.height * 0.5)
                    )
                    .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
                }
            }
            // Reduce Motion: keep the glare and the lift, drop the rotation.
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(Double(-tilt.height) * angle), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0))
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(Double(tilt.width) * angle), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0))
            .scaleEffect(isDragging ? 1.03 : 1)
            .gesture(
                DragGesture()
                    .onChanged { value in
                        withAnimation(.interactiveSpring()) {
                            isDragging = true
                            tilt = CGSize(
                                width: clamp(value.translation.width / range),
                                height: clamp(value.translation.height / range)
                            )
                        }
                    }
                    .onEnded { _ in
                        withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.55)) {
                            isDragging = false
                            tilt = .zero
                        }
                    }
            )
    }

    private var angle: Double { reduceMotion ? 0 : maxAngle }

    private func clamp(_ value: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        min(1, max(-1, value))
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Tilts the view in 3D while it is dragged.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// CardView()
    ///     .tiltOnDrag(maxAngle: 15, cornerRadius: 20)
    /// ```
    func tiltOnDrag(maxAngle: Double = 12, glare: Bool = true, cornerRadius: CGFloat = 16) -> some View {
        modifier(TiltModifier(maxAngle: maxAngle, glare: glare, cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)
        .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [.purple, .blue], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
        .frame(width: 220, height: 300)
        .tiltOnDrag(cornerRadius: 20)
        .padding(40)
}
```

## Scroll Reveal (`scroll-reveal`)

Rows scale up and come into focus as they enter the visible area.

- API: `.scrollReveal()`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ScrollReveal.swift

### Usage

```swift
ScrollView {
    LazyVStack {
        ForEach(items) { item in
            Row(item).scrollReveal()
        }
    }
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .scrollReveal() view modifier (iOS 17+) using scrollTransition(.interactive). When an item is fully inside the scroll view (phase.isIdentity) it is at full opacity, scale 1 and no blur; as it moves toward the top or bottom edge it interpolates to opacity 0.3, scale 0.85 and a 2 pt blur. Axis, minimum scale, minimum opacity and blur amount should be parameters.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

public extension View {
    /// Items scale up and come into focus as they scroll into the visible
    /// area, and fade back out as they leave. Use inside a `ScrollView`.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ScrollView {
    ///     LazyVStack {
    ///         ForEach(items) { item in
    ///             Row(item).scrollReveal()
    ///         }
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    func scrollReveal(
        axis: Axis = .vertical,
        minScale: CGFloat = 0.85,
        minOpacity: Double = 0.3,
        blur: CGFloat = 2
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ScrollRevealModifier(axis: axis, minScale: minScale, minOpacity: minOpacity, blur: blur))
    }
}

struct ScrollRevealModifier: ViewModifier {
    var axis: Axis
    var minScale: CGFloat
    var minOpacity: Double
    var blur: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Reduce Motion: keep the fade, drop the scaling and blur.
        let minScale = reduceMotion ? 1 : minScale
        let blur = reduceMotion ? 0 : blur
        let minOpacity = minOpacity
        return content.scrollTransition(.interactive, axis: axis) { view, phase in
            view
                .opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : minOpacity)
                .scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : minScale)
                .blur(radius: phase.isIdentity ? 0 : blur)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScrollView {
        LazyVStack(spacing: 12) {
            ForEach(0..<30, id: \.self) { index in
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14)
                    .fill(Color.accentColor.gradient)
                    .frame(height: 80)
                    .overlay(Text("Row \(index)").foregroundStyle(.white))
                    .scrollReveal()
            }
        }
        .padding()
    }
}
```

## Flip Card (`flip-card`)

A two-sided card turns over in 3D with a spring.

- API: `FlipCard(isFlipped:) { } back: { }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/FlipCard.swift

### Usage

```swift
@State private var flipped = false

FlipCard(isFlipped: flipped) {
    QuestionView()
} back: {
    AnswerView()
}
.frame(width: 220, height: 300)
.onTapGesture { flipped.toggle() }
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI FlipCard<Front, Back> view (iOS 17+) with isFlipped and axis (horizontal or vertical) parameters and front/back view builders. Stack both faces in a ZStack and give each an Animatable view modifier holding the animated angle (0 or 180°). The back face uses angle − 180 so it reads correctly once turned. Each face applies rotation3DEffect around the y axis (or x for vertical) with perspective 0.5 and sets opacity to 1 only while |faceAngle| < 90°, so the faces swap exactly at the halfway point and the back never shows mirrored. Animate isFlipped changes with spring(response 0.6, damping 0.75). Hide the hidden face from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on, cross-fade instead of rotating.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A two-sided card that turns over in 3D, showing `back` when `isFlipped`
/// is true. The faces swap exactly at 90°, so the back never shows mirrored.
public struct FlipCard<Front: View, Back: View>: View {
    private let isFlipped: Bool
    private let axis: Axis
    private let front: Front
    private let back: Back

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isFlipped: Shows the back when true.
    ///   - axis: `.horizontal` turns like a page (around the vertical axis),
    ///     `.vertical` tumbles top over bottom.
    public init(
        isFlipped: Bool,
        axis: Axis = .horizontal,
        @ViewBuilder front: () -> Front,
        @ViewBuilder back: () -> Back
    ) {
        self.isFlipped = isFlipped
        self.axis = axis
        self.front = front()
        self.back = back()
    }

    public var body: some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            // Cross-fade instead of turning.
            ZStack {
                front.opacity(isFlipped ? 0 : 1)
                back.opacity(isFlipped ? 1 : 0)
            }
            .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3), value: isFlipped)
        } else {
            ZStack {
                front.modifier(FlipFace(angle: isFlipped ? 180 : 0, axis: axis, isBack: false))
                back.modifier(FlipFace(angle: isFlipped ? 180 : 0, axis: axis, isBack: true))
            }
            .animation(.spring(response: 0.6, dampingFraction: 0.75), value: isFlipped)
        }
    }
}

/// Rotates one face by `angle` and hides it while it faces away.
private struct FlipFace: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var angle: Double
    var axis: Axis
    var isBack: Bool

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { angle }
        set { angle = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // The back starts already turned 180° so it reads correctly when shown.
        let faceAngle = isBack ? angle - 180 : angle
        let visible = abs(faceAngle) < 90
        content
            .opacity(visible ? 1 : 0)
            .accessibilityHidden(!visible)
            .rotation3DEffect(
                .degrees(faceAngle),
                axis: axis == .horizontal ? (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0) : (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0),
                perspective: 0.5
            )
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var flipped = false

        var body: some View {
            FlipCard(isFlipped: flipped) {
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20).fill(.blue.gradient)
                    .overlay(Text("Front").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
            } back: {
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20).fill(.orange.gradient)
                    .overlay(Text("Back").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
            }
            .frame(width: 200, height: 260)
            .onTapGesture { flipped.toggle() }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Swipe Card Stack (`swipe-stack`)

Tinder-style deck: drag the top card away and the pile moves up.

- API: `SwipeCardStack(items) { item in }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/SwipeCardStack.swift

### Usage

```swift
SwipeCardStack(profiles) { profile, direction in
    direction == .right ? like(profile) : pass(profile)
} card: { profile in
    ProfileCard(profile)
        .frame(width: 300, height: 420)
}
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI SwipeCardStack (iOS 17+) over a collection of Identifiable items with a card view builder and an onSwipe(item, direction) callback. Show the top 3 cards from the current position (looping by default). Cards behind are scaled down 5% per level and moved down 12 pt per level. The top card follows a DragGesture: offset by the translation, rotate by translation.width / 20 degrees around the bottom anchor, and overlay a green (right) or red (left) wash, masked by the card, whose opacity grows to 25% at the threshold. On release, if the predicted end translation passes 110 pt, fly the card 600 pt off in that direction with easeIn(0.25), then reset the drag without animation, advance the position with a spring so the pile moves up, and call onSwipe. Otherwise spring back. Add Swipe left and Swipe right accessibility actions.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Which way a card left the stack.
public enum SwipeDirection: Sendable {
    case left
    case right
}

/// A Tinder-style deck. The top card follows the finger and tilts; past a
/// threshold it flies off and the cards behind move up. Drag less and it
/// springs back.
public struct SwipeCardStack<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Card: View>: View where Data.Element: Identifiable {
    private let items: Data
    private let visibleCount: Int
    private let loops: Bool
    private let onSwipe: (Data.Element, SwipeDirection) -> Void
    private let card: (Data.Element) -> Card

    @State private var position = 0
    @State private var drag: CGSize = .zero
    @State private var flyingOff: SwipeDirection?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let threshold: CGFloat = 110

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: The cards, top card first.
    ///   - visibleCount: How many cards are drawn in the pile.
    ///   - loops: Starts over from the first card when the deck runs out.
    ///   - onSwipe: Called after a card leaves, with the direction it went.
    ///   - card: Builds the view for one item.
    public init(
        _ items: Data,
        visibleCount: Int = 3,
        loops: Bool = true,
        onSwipe: @escaping (Data.Element, SwipeDirection) -> Void = { _, _ in },
        @ViewBuilder card: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Card
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.visibleCount = visibleCount
        self.loops = loops
        self.onSwipe = onSwipe
        self.card = card
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let elements = Array(items)
        ZStack {
            ForEach(Array(visibleCards(elements).enumerated()).reversed(), id: \.element.id) { depth, item in
                card(item)
                    .modifier(StackedCard(depth: depth, drag: depth == 0 ? drag : .zero, threshold: threshold))
                    .allowsHitTesting(depth == 0)
                    .gesture(depth == 0 ? dragGesture(for: item) : nil)
                    .accessibilityHidden(depth != 0)
                    .accessibilityActions {
                        Button("Swipe left") { swipe(item, .left) }
                        Button("Swipe right") { swipe(item, .right) }
                    }
            }
        }
    }

    private func visibleCards(_ elements: [Data.Element]) -> [Data.Element] {
        guard !elements.isEmpty else { return [] }
        let remaining = loops ? elements.count : max(0, elements.count - position)
        return (0..<min(visibleCount, remaining)).map { elements[(position + $0) % elements.count] }
    }

    private func dragGesture(for item: Data.Element) -> some Gesture {
        DragGesture()
            .onChanged { value in
                guard flyingOff == nil else { return }
                drag = value.translation
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                guard flyingOff == nil else { return }
                // Use the predicted end so a quick flick counts too.
                let x = value.predictedEndTranslation.width
                if abs(x) > threshold {
                    swipe(item, x > 0 ? .right : .left)
                } else {
                    withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.6)) { drag = .zero }
                }
            }
    }

    private func swipe(_ item: Data.Element, _ direction: SwipeDirection) {
        flyingOff = direction
        let distance: CGFloat = direction == .right ? 600 : -600
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.2) : .easeIn(duration: 0.25)) {
            drag = CGSize(width: distance, height: drag.height + 40)
        }
        DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.25) {
            var transaction = Transaction()
            transaction.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(transaction) { drag = .zero }
            withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.8)) { position += 1 }
            flyingOff = nil
            onSwipe(item, direction)
        }
    }
}

/// Places a card in the pile: deeper cards are smaller and lower; the top
/// card follows the drag and tilts away from it.
private struct StackedCard: ViewModifier {
    var depth: Int
    var drag: CGSize
    var threshold: CGFloat

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                // Green or red wash that grows as the card nears the threshold.
                let progress = min(1, abs(drag.width) / threshold)
                (drag.width > 0 ? Color.green : Color.red)
                    .opacity(depth == 0 ? Double(progress) * 0.25 : 0)
                    .mask { content }
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
            .scaleEffect(1 - CGFloat(depth) * 0.05)
            .offset(y: CGFloat(depth) * 12)
            .offset(drag)
            .rotationEffect(.degrees(Double(drag.width / 20)), anchor: .bottom)
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Item: Identifiable {
        let id: Int
        let color: Color
    }
    let items = [Color.pink, .orange, .teal, .indigo].enumerated().map { Item(id: $0, color: $1) }
    return SwipeCardStack(items) { item in
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)
            .fill(item.color.gradient)
            .frame(width: 220, height: 300)
            .overlay(Text("Card \(item.id + 1)").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
    }
    .padding(40)
}
```

## Parallax Carousel (`parallax-carousel`)

Paging cards whose images slide slower than the cards, for depth.

- API: `ParallaxCarousel(items) { item in }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ParallaxCarousel.swift

### Usage

```swift
ParallaxCarousel(places) { place in
    Image(place.photo)
        .resizable()
        .scaledToFill()
}
.frame(height: 240)
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI ParallaxCarousel (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with an optional selection binding. Use a horizontal ScrollView with a LazyHStack (14 pt spacing), .scrollTargetLayout(), .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), hidden indicators, .scrollPosition(id:anchor: .center), and horizontal contentMargins so each card (78% of the width) snaps to the centre with neighbours peeking. Draw each card's content wider than the card by the parallax factor (0.35), then use .visualEffect to read the card's frame in the .scrollView coordinate space and offset the content by −(distance of the card centre from the viewport centre) × parallax. Finally frame it to the card size and clip it with a continuous rounded rectangle (22 pt), so the image appears to move slower than its frame. With Reduce Motion on, set parallax to 0.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A paging carousel whose card contents slide slower than the cards
/// themselves, so images seem to sit deeper than the frame around them.
/// Neighbouring cards peek in from both sides.
public struct ParallaxCarousel<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Content: View>: View where Data.Element: Identifiable {
    private let items: Data
    private let selection: Binding<Data.Element.ID?>?
    private let cardWidth: CGFloat
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let cornerRadius: CGFloat
    private let parallax: CGFloat
    private let content: (Data.Element) -> Content

    @State private var internalSelection: Data.Element.ID?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: One card per item.
    ///   - selection: Optional binding to the centred card; set it to scroll.
    ///   - cardWidth: Card width as a fraction of the carousel's width.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between cards.
    ///   - cornerRadius: Corner radius of each card.
    ///   - parallax: How much slower the content moves than its card (0…1).
    ///   - content: The card's content, usually an image. It is drawn wider
    ///     than the card so the parallax never reveals an edge.
    public init(
        _ items: Data,
        selection: Binding<Data.Element.ID?>? = nil,
        cardWidth: CGFloat = 0.78,
        spacing: CGFloat = 14,
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 22,
        parallax: CGFloat = 0.35,
        @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Content
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.selection = selection
        self.cardWidth = cardWidth
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.cornerRadius = cornerRadius
        self.parallax = parallax
        self.content = content
    }

    public var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let width = geometry.size.width * cardWidth
            let strength = reduceMotion ? 0 : parallax
            ScrollView(.horizontal) {
                LazyHStack(spacing: spacing) {
                    ForEach(items) { item in
                        content(item)
                            // Extra width on both sides for the content to slide into.
                            .frame(width: width * (1 + strength), height: geometry.size.height)
                            .visualEffect { view, proxy in
                                // How far this card's centre is from the carousel's centre.
                                let frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal))
                                let viewport = proxy.bounds(of: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal))?.width ?? frame.width
                                let distance = frame.midX - viewport / 2
                                return view.offset(x: -distance * strength)
                            }
                            .frame(width: width, height: geometry.size.height)
                            .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
                            .id(item.id)
                    }
                }
                .scrollTargetLayout()
            }
            .contentMargins(.horizontal, (geometry.size.width - width) / 2, for: .scrollContent)
            .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)
            .scrollIndicators(.hidden)
            .scrollPosition(id: selection ?? $internalSelection, anchor: .center)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Place: Identifiable {
        let id: Int
        let colors: [Color]
    }
    let places = [
        Place(id: 0, colors: [.orange, .pink]),
        Place(id: 1, colors: [.teal, .blue]),
        Place(id: 2, colors: [.purple, .indigo]),
        Place(id: 3, colors: [.mint, .green]),
    ]
    return ParallaxCarousel(places) { place in
        LinearGradient(colors: place.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
            .overlay(Image(systemName: "mountain.2.fill").font(.system(size: 60)).foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.8)))
    }
    .frame(height: 220)
}
```

## Expandable Card (`expandable-card`)

Tap the header and the card springs open, un-blurring its detail.

- API: `ExpandableCard(isExpanded:) { } detail: { }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ExpandableCard.swift

### Usage

```swift
@State private var isOpen = false

ExpandableCard(isExpanded: $isOpen) {
    Text("Shipping").font(.headline)
} detail: {
    Text("Arrives Thursday. Free returns within 30 days.")
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI ExpandableCard<Header, Detail> (iOS 17+) bound to isExpanded. A VStack holds a plain-style Button containing the header, a spacer and a chevron.down that rotates −180° when open, then, if expanded, the detail view. Toggle inside withAnimation(.spring(response 0.45, damping 0.8)) so the card's height springs. Insert the detail with a combined transition of opacity, an 8 pt upward offset and a custom blur transition (radius 6 → 0). The background is a continuous rounded rectangle (16 pt) filled with the background style whose shadow deepens when open. Expose Expanded/Collapsed as the accessibility value. With Reduce Motion on, use a short ease and an opacity transition only.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A card with a tappable header that expands to reveal its detail. The
/// height springs open, the chevron turns, and the detail un-blurs into place.
/// Stack several for an accordion.
public struct ExpandableCard<Header: View, Detail: View>: View {
    @Binding private var isExpanded: Bool
    private let cornerRadius: CGFloat
    private let header: Header
    private let detail: Detail

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isExpanded: Whether the detail is showing.
    ///   - cornerRadius: Corner radius of the card.
    ///   - header: Always visible; tapping it toggles the card.
    ///   - detail: Shown below the header when expanded.
    public init(
        isExpanded: Binding<Bool>,
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 16,
        @ViewBuilder header: () -> Header,
        @ViewBuilder detail: () -> Detail
    ) {
        _isExpanded = isExpanded
        self.cornerRadius = cornerRadius
        self.header = header()
        self.detail = detail()
    }

    public var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
            Button {
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.8)) {
                    isExpanded.toggle()
                }
            } label: {
                HStack {
                    header
                    Spacer(minLength: 8)
                    Image(systemName: "chevron.down")
                        .font(.footnote.weight(.semibold))
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                        .rotationEffect(.degrees(isExpanded ? -180 : 0))
                }
                .padding()
                .contentShape(Rectangle())
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .accessibilityValue(isExpanded ? Text("Expanded") : Text("Collapsed"))

            if isExpanded {
                detail
                    .padding([.horizontal, .bottom])
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                    .transition(
                        reduceMotion
                            ? .opacity
                            : .opacity.combined(with: .offset(y: -8)).combined(with: BlurTransition.blur)
                    )
            }
        }
        .background(
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous)
                .fill(.background)
                .shadow(color: .black.opacity(isExpanded ? 0.12 : 0.06), radius: isExpanded ? 12 : 4, y: isExpanded ? 6 : 2)
        )
        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
    }
}

/// Blurs a view while it is inserted or removed.
private struct BlurTransition: ViewModifier {
    var radius: CGFloat

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.blur(radius: radius)
    }

    static var blur: AnyTransition {
        .modifier(active: BlurTransition(radius: 6), identity: BlurTransition(radius: 0))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var open = [true, false, false]

        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 12) {
                ForEach(0..<3) { index in
                    ExpandableCard(isExpanded: $open[index]) {
                        Text("Question \(index + 1)").font(.headline)
                    } detail: {
                        Text("Answers expand smoothly with a spring, and the detail fades and un-blurs into place.")
                            .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    }
                }
            }
            .padding()
            .background(Color.gray.opacity(0.1))
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Hero Expand (`hero-expand`)

A thumbnail grows into a full detail card, morphing with matchedGeometryEffect.

- API: `HeroGrid(items) { thumbnail } detail: { }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/HeroGrid.swift

### Usage

```swift
HeroGrid(photos, columns: 3) { photo in
    Image(photo.thumbnail).resizable().scaledToFill().frame(height: 90)
} detail: { photo in
    PhotoDetail(photo)
}
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI HeroGrid (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with columns (3), spacing (10), cornerRadius (14) and two view builders: thumbnail and detail. Keep @State selected: Item.ID? and a @Namespace. In a ZStack, show a LazyVGrid of flexible columns; for each item, if it isn't selected show a plain Button with the thumbnail clipped to a continuous rounded rectangle and .matchedGeometryEffect(id: item.id, in: namespace), otherwise show the thumbnail .hidden() to keep the slot. Dim the grid to 30 % while something is selected. Above it, if selected, show the detail in a Button sized maxWidth/maxHeight .infinity, clipped the same way, with the same matchedGeometryEffect id and zIndex 1. Open with withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.82)) and close by tapping the detail. Both views get an .opacity transition so their content cross-fades while the frame morphs. With Reduce Motion on, pass properties: [] to matchedGeometryEffect so it only cross-fades.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A grid of thumbnails where tapping one grows it into a detail card that
/// fills the grid, morphing frame and corners with `matchedGeometryEffect`.
/// Tapping the detail shrinks it back into its slot.
public struct HeroGrid<Item: Identifiable, Thumbnail: View, Detail: View>: View {
    private let items: [Item]
    private let columns: Int
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let cornerRadius: CGFloat
    private let thumbnail: (Item) -> Thumbnail
    private let detail: (Item) -> Detail

    @State private var selected: Item.ID?
    @Namespace private var namespace
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: The items to show.
    ///   - columns: Number of grid columns.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between cells, in points.
    ///   - cornerRadius: Corner radius of thumbnails and the detail card.
    ///   - thumbnail: The small cell for an item. Give it a background so the
    ///     morph has something to stretch.
    ///   - detail: The expanded card for an item.
    public init(
        _ items: [Item],
        columns: Int = 3,
        spacing: CGFloat = 10,
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 14,
        @ViewBuilder thumbnail: @escaping (Item) -> Thumbnail,
        @ViewBuilder detail: @escaping (Item) -> Detail
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.columns = columns
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.cornerRadius = cornerRadius
        self.thumbnail = thumbnail
        self.detail = detail
    }

    public var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: cross-fade in place of the morph.
        let morph: MatchedGeometryProperties = reduceMotion ? [] : .frame
        ZStack {
            LazyVGrid(columns: Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: spacing), count: max(1, columns)), spacing: spacing) {
                ForEach(items) { item in
                    ZStack {
                        if selected != item.id {
                            Button { open(item.id) } label: {
                                thumbnail(item)
                                    .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
                            }
                            .buttonStyle(.plain)
                            .matchedGeometryEffect(id: item.id, in: namespace, properties: morph)
                            .transition(.opacity.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.15)))
                        } else {
                            // Keep the slot so the grid doesn't reflow.
                            thumbnail(item).hidden()
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            .opacity(selected == nil ? 1 : 0.3)

            if let id = selected, let item = items.first(where: { $0.id == id }) {
                Button { close() } label: {
                    detail(item)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
                        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
                .matchedGeometryEffect(id: id, in: namespace, properties: morph)
                .transition(.opacity.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.15)))
                .zIndex(1)
            }
        }
    }

    private func open(_ id: Item.ID) {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.25) : .spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.82)) {
            selected = id
        }
    }

    private func close() {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.25) : .spring(response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.85)) {
            selected = nil
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Tile: Identifiable {
        let id: Int
        let color: Color
    }
    let tiles = [Color.pink, .orange, .teal, .indigo, .mint, .purple].enumerated().map { Tile(id: $0.offset, color: $0.element) }
    return HeroGrid(tiles) { tile in
        tile.color.frame(height: 70)
    } detail: { tile in
        tile.color.overlay(Text("Tile \(tile.id + 1)").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
    }
    .frame(width: 300, height: 160)
    .padding()
}
```

## Spotlight Card (`spotlight-card`)

A soft glow follows the pointer across the card, like a torch.

- API: `.spotlight()`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Hover / Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/Spotlight.swift

### Usage

```swift
FeatureCard()
    .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20))
    .spotlight()

PricingCard()
    .spotlight(color: .purple.opacity(0.4), radius: 160)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .spotlight(color:radius:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Track the pointer with .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) and a finger with a simultaneous DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0); store the location in @State (nil when the pointer leaves or the drag ends) and remember the last location so the glow can fade out where it was. In an overlay GeometryReader, draw a RadialGradient from color (white 35 %) to clear, centred at the location converted to a UnitPoint, endRadius = radius (120 pt), and mask it with the content so it only lights the card. Move with .interactiveSpring(response: 0.2, dampingFraction: 0.9) and fade out with easeOut(0.35 s). Disable hit testing on the glow. With Reduce Motion on, move the glow without animation.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A soft glow that follows the pointer (or a dragging finger) across the
/// view, like a torch shone on the card. Fades out when the pointer leaves.
struct SpotlightModifier: ViewModifier {
    var color: Color
    var radius: CGFloat

    @State private var location: CGPoint?
    @State private var lastLocation: CGPoint = .zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                GeometryReader { geometry in
                    let size = geometry.size
                    let point = location ?? lastLocation
                    RadialGradient(
                        colors: [color, color.opacity(0)],
                        center: UnitPoint(x: size.width > 0 ? point.x / size.width : 0.5,
                                          y: size.height > 0 ? point.y / size.height : 0.5),
                        startRadius: 0,
                        endRadius: radius
                    )
                    .opacity(location == nil ? 0 : 1)
                }
                .mask { content }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) { phase in
                switch phase {
                case let .active(point): move(to: point)
                case .ended: hide()
                }
            }
            .simultaneousGesture(
                DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0, coordinateSpace: .local)
                    .onChanged { move(to: $0.location) }
                    .onEnded { _ in hide() }
            )
    }

    private func move(to point: CGPoint) {
        // Reduce Motion: no glide, the glow jumps with the pointer.
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .interactiveSpring(response: 0.2, dampingFraction: 0.9)) {
            location = point
            lastLocation = point
        }
    }

    private func hide() {
        withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.35)) { location = nil }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Shines a soft glow on the view where the pointer or finger is.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// FeatureCard()
    ///     .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20))
    ///     .spotlight()
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - color: Colour at the centre of the glow.
    ///   - radius: Radius of the glow, in points.
    func spotlight(color: Color = .white.opacity(0.35), radius: CGFloat = 120) -> some View {
        modifier(SpotlightModifier(color: color, radius: radius))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)
        .fill(Color(white: 0.1))
        .frame(width: 260, height: 160)
        .overlay(Text("Hover me").font(.headline).foregroundStyle(.white))
        .spotlight()
        .padding()
}
```
