## Film Grain (`grain`)

Flickering film grain over any view, from a tiled noise texture.

- API: `.grain()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/Grain.swift

### Usage

```swift
LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
    .grain()

HeroImage()
    .grain(opacity: 0.2, isAnimated: false)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .grain(opacity:isAnimated:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Generate a 128 × 128 grey noise CGImage once (8-bit DeviceGray, random bytes from a seeded generator, no interpolation). In an overlay, show it with Image(decorative:scale: 2).resizable(resizingMode: .tile) in a frame 64 pt larger than the view in each direction, clipped, and shift it by a different offset (frame × 37 mod 64, frame × 53 mod 64) 12 times a second using TimelineView(.periodic(by: 1/12)), so the grain flickers like film. Use .blendMode(.overlay) at opacity (0.35), disable hit testing and hide it from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on (or isAnimated false), keep the grain still.

### Source

```swift
import CoreGraphics
import SwiftUI

/// Film grain: a tiled noise texture over the view, re-positioned a few times
/// a second so it flickers like real film.
struct GrainModifier: ViewModifier {
    var opacity: Double
    var isAnimated: Bool

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.overlay {
            if let noise = NoiseTexture.image {
                // Reduce Motion: still grain.
                let animated = isAnimated && !reduceMotion
                TimelineView(.periodic(from: .now, by: 1.0 / 12)) { timeline in
                    let frame = animated ? Int(timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * 12) : 0
                    GeometryReader { geometry in
                        Image(decorative: noise, scale: 2)
                            .resizable(resizingMode: .tile)
                            // One tile larger than the view in each direction so
                            // the random shift never uncovers an edge.
                            .frame(width: geometry.size.width + 64, height: geometry.size.height + 64)
                            .offset(x: -CGFloat(frame * 37 % 64), y: -CGFloat(frame * 53 % 64))
                    }
                    .clipped()
                }
                .blendMode(.overlay)
                .opacity(opacity)
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A 128×128 grey noise image, generated once.
enum NoiseTexture {
    static let image: CGImage? = {
        let side = 128
        var generator = SplitMix64(seed: 7)
        var pixels = [UInt8](repeating: 0, count: side * side)
        for index in pixels.indices {
            pixels[index] = UInt8(truncatingIfNeeded: generator.next() >> 56)
        }
        guard let provider = CGDataProvider(data: Data(pixels) as CFData) else { return nil }
        return CGImage(
            width: side,
            height: side,
            bitsPerComponent: 8,
            bitsPerPixel: 8,
            bytesPerRow: side,
            space: CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceGray(),
            bitmapInfo: CGBitmapInfo(rawValue: CGImageAlphaInfo.none.rawValue),
            provider: provider,
            decode: nil,
            shouldInterpolate: false,
            intent: .defaultIntent
        )
    }()
}

public extension View {
    /// Lays flickering film grain over the view.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
    ///     .grain()
    ///
    /// HeroImage()
    ///     .grain(opacity: 0.25, isAnimated: false)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - opacity: Strength of the grain (0…1).
    ///   - isAnimated: Re-rolls the grain 12 times a second when true.
    func grain(opacity: Double = 0.35, isAnimated: Bool = true) -> some View {
        modifier(GrainModifier(opacity: opacity, isAnimated: isAnimated))
    }
}

#Preview {
    LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink, .purple], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
        .grain()
        .frame(width: 300, height: 200)
}
```

## Flashlight (`flashlight`)

The view goes dark except a soft circle of light around the pointer.

- API: `.flashlight()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Hover / Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/Flashlight.swift

### Usage

```swift
TreasureMap()
    .flashlight(radius: 100)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .flashlight(radius:darkness:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Track the pointer with .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) and a finger with a simultaneous DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0), storing the location in @State (nil on exit) plus the last location. In an overlay GeometryReader, draw a RadialGradient from clear to black at darkness (0.85) opacity, centred on the location as a UnitPoint, from startRadius 0.55 × radius to endRadius radius (90 pt), so everything outside the circle is dark with a soft edge. Fade the whole overlay out when the pointer leaves (lights back on) with easeOut(0.4 s), and follow the pointer with .interactiveSpring(response: 0.18). Disable hit testing. With Reduce Motion on, move without animation.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Darkens the view except for a soft circle of light around the pointer (or
/// a dragging finger), like exploring a dark room with a torch.
struct FlashlightModifier: ViewModifier {
    var radius: CGFloat
    var darkness: Double

    @State private var location: CGPoint?
    @State private var lastLocation: CGPoint?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                GeometryReader { geometry in
                    let size = geometry.size
                    let point = location ?? lastLocation ?? CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
                    RadialGradient(
                        colors: [.black.opacity(0), .black.opacity(darkness)],
                        center: UnitPoint(x: size.width > 0 ? point.x / size.width : 0.5,
                                          y: size.height > 0 ? point.y / size.height : 0.5),
                        startRadius: radius * 0.55,
                        endRadius: radius
                    )
                    // Lights come back on when the pointer leaves.
                    .opacity(location == nil ? 0 : 1)
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) { phase in
                switch phase {
                case let .active(point): move(to: point)
                case .ended: release()
                }
            }
            .simultaneousGesture(
                DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0, coordinateSpace: .local)
                    .onChanged { move(to: $0.location) }
                    .onEnded { _ in release() }
            )
    }

    private func move(to point: CGPoint) {
        // Reduce Motion: the light jumps with the pointer instead of trailing it.
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .interactiveSpring(response: 0.18, dampingFraction: 0.9)) {
            location = point
            lastLocation = point
        }
    }

    private func release() {
        withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.4)) { location = nil }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Dims the view except around the pointer or finger.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// TreasureMap()
    ///     .flashlight(radius: 100)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - radius: Radius of the lit circle, in points.
    ///   - darkness: Opacity of the darkness outside the light (0…1).
    func flashlight(radius: CGFloat = 90, darkness: Double = 0.85) -> some View {
        modifier(FlashlightModifier(radius: radius, darkness: darkness))
    }
}

#Preview {
    LinearGradient(colors: [.yellow, .orange, .red], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
        .overlay(Text("Find me").font(.largeTitle.bold()))
        .frame(width: 300, height: 200)
        .flashlight()
}
```

## Rolling Number (`rolling-number`)

Digits roll like an odometer when the value changes.

- API: `RollingNumber(value:)`
- Component: Number
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/RollingNumber.swift

### Usage

```swift
RollingNumber(value: score)
    .font(.system(size: 48, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI RollingNumber view (iOS 17+) that displays a number with odometer-style digit rolling. Render Text(value, format:) with monospacedDigit(), apply .contentTransition(.numericText(value:)) so digits roll up when the value increases and down when it decreases, and animate changes with .snappy. Provide initialisers for Int and for Double with a FloatingPointFormatStyle.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A number whose digits roll up or down when the value changes, like an
/// odometer. Built on `contentTransition(.numericText)`.
///
/// ```swift
/// RollingNumber(value: score)
///     .font(.system(size: 48, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
/// ```
public struct RollingNumber: View {
    private let value: Double
    private let format: FloatingPointFormatStyle<Double>
    private let animation: Animation

    public init(
        value: Double,
        format: FloatingPointFormatStyle<Double> = .number.precision(.fractionLength(0)),
        animation: Animation = .snappy
    ) {
        self.value = value
        self.format = format
        self.animation = animation
    }

    public init(value: Int, animation: Animation = .snappy) {
        self.init(value: Double(value), animation: animation)
    }

    public var body: some View {
        Text(value, format: format)
            .monospacedDigit()
            .contentTransition(.numericText(value: value))
            .animation(animation, value: value)
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var value = 1280
        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                RollingNumber(value: value)
                    .font(.system(size: 56, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
                HStack {
                    Button("-") { value -= Int.random(in: 1...300) }
                    Button("+") { value += Int.random(in: 1...300) }
                }
                .buttonStyle(.bordered)
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Particle Field (`particle-field`)

Drifting particles linked by faint lines, like a living constellation.

- API: `ParticleField()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/ParticleField.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack {
    Color.black.ignoresSafeArea()
    ParticleField(count: 60, color: .cyan)
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    Text("Connected").font(.largeTitle.bold())
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI ParticleField view (iOS 17+) with count (50), color, speed (14 pt/s) and linkDistance (70 pt). Generate each particle's traits once from a seeded SplitMix64 generator: start position (0…1 in each axis), direction, speed factor (0.4–1.2), radius (1–2.8 pt) and opacity (0.4–1). In TimelineView(.animation) with a Canvas, compute each position as start + direction × time × speed × factor, wrapped around the canvas edges, so there is no stored state. Stroke a 0.8 pt line between every pair closer than linkDistance with opacity 0.35 × (1 − distance / linkDistance), then fill each particle as a circle. Hide it from accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, freeze time.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Particles drifting slowly through the view, joined by faint lines when they
/// come close, like a constellation. A calm, techy background.
public struct ParticleField: View {
    private let count: Int
    private let color: Color
    private let speed: Double
    private let linkDistance: CGFloat
    private let seeds: [ParticleSeed]

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - count: Number of particles.
    ///   - color: Particle and line colour.
    ///   - speed: Drift speed in points per second.
    ///   - linkDistance: Particles closer than this are joined by a line (0 turns lines off).
    public init(count: Int = 50, color: Color = .white, speed: Double = 14, linkDistance: CGFloat = 70) {
        self.count = count
        self.color = color
        self.speed = speed
        self.linkDistance = linkDistance
        var generator = SplitMix64(seed: 42)
        seeds = (0..<max(0, count)).map { _ in ParticleSeed(using: &generator) }
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            Canvas { context, size in
                let positions = seeds.map { $0.position(at: time, speed: speed, in: size) }
                if linkDistance > 0 {
                    for i in positions.indices {
                        for j in positions.indices where j > i {
                            let distance = hypot(positions[i].x - positions[j].x, positions[i].y - positions[j].y)
                            guard distance < linkDistance else { continue }
                            var line = Path()
                            line.move(to: positions[i])
                            line.addLine(to: positions[j])
                            context.stroke(line, with: .color(color.opacity(0.35 * (1 - distance / linkDistance))), lineWidth: 0.8)
                        }
                    }
                }
                for (seed, point) in zip(seeds, positions) {
                    let r = seed.radius
                    context.fill(
                        Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: point.x - r, y: point.y - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2)),
                        with: .color(color.opacity(seed.opacity))
                    )
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

/// Fixed random traits of one particle. Its position is a pure function of
/// time, so the field needs no state and never drifts out of the view.
struct ParticleSeed {
    var start: CGPoint      // 0…1 in both axes
    var direction: Double   // radians
    var speedFactor: Double
    var radius: CGFloat
    var opacity: Double

    init(using generator: inout SplitMix64) {
        start = CGPoint(x: generator.unit(), y: generator.unit())
        direction = generator.unit() * 2 * .pi
        speedFactor = 0.4 + generator.unit() * 0.8
        radius = 1 + generator.unit() * 1.8
        opacity = 0.4 + generator.unit() * 0.6
    }

    func position(at time: Double, speed: Double, in size: CGSize) -> CGPoint {
        guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0 else { return .zero }
        let travel = time * speed * speedFactor
        let x = (start.x * size.width + CGFloat(cos(direction) * travel)).wrapped(to: size.width)
        let y = (start.y * size.height + CGFloat(sin(direction) * travel)).wrapped(to: size.height)
        return CGPoint(x: x, y: y)
    }
}

/// Small deterministic random generator, so particle layouts are stable
/// between launches and previews.
struct SplitMix64: RandomNumberGenerator {
    private var state: UInt64

    init(seed: UInt64) { state = seed }

    mutating func next() -> UInt64 {
        state &+= 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15
        var z = state
        z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) &* 0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9
        z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) &* 0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB
        return z ^ (z >> 31)
    }

    /// A Double in 0..<1.
    mutating func unit() -> Double { Double.random(in: 0..<1, using: &self) }
}

extension CGFloat {
    /// Wraps the value into 0..<length.
    func wrapped(to length: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        let r = truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: length)
        return r < 0 ? r + length : r
    }
}

#Preview {
    ParticleField()
        .background(Color(red: 0.05, green: 0.07, blue: 0.15))
        .frame(width: 320, height: 220)
}
```

## Starfield (`starfield`)

Stars stream out of the centre and stretch into streaks: warp speed.

- API: `Starfield()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Starfield.swift

### Usage

```swift
Starfield()
    .background(.black)
    .ignoresSafeArea()

Starfield(count: 300, speed: 1.5) // warp jump
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Starfield view (iOS 17+) with count (200), speed (0.35 depth units per second) and color. Give each star a seeded random x and y in −1…1 and a depth in 0…1. In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), compute z = 0.05 + 0.95 × fract(depth − time × speed), so stars approach the camera and wrap back to the far plane. Project with perspective: point = centre + (x, y) / z × 0.15 × half the larger side. Draw each star as a round-capped streak from its projection at a slightly larger z (z + min(0.08, speed × 0.05)) to its current projection, with opacity and line width growing as it gets closer. Hide it from accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, freeze time.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Flying through space: stars stream out from the centre and stretch into
/// streaks as they pass the camera. Raise `speed` for a warp jump.
public struct Starfield: View {
    private let speed: Double
    private let color: Color
    private let stars: [Star]

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - count: Number of stars.
    ///   - speed: Depth units per second; 0.3 cruises, 1.5 is warp speed.
    ///   - color: Star colour.
    public init(count: Int = 200, speed: Double = 0.35, color: Color = .white) {
        self.speed = speed
        self.color = color
        var generator = SplitMix64(seed: 7)
        stars = (0..<max(0, count)).map { _ in
            Star(
                x: generator.unit() * 2 - 1,
                y: generator.unit() * 2 - 1,
                depth: generator.unit()
            )
        }
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            Canvas { context, size in
                let centre = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
                let scale = max(size.width, size.height) * 0.5
                // Streak length: where the star was a moment ago.
                let trail = min(0.08, speed * 0.05)
                for star in stars {
                    // Depth runs 1 (far) → 0.05 (at the camera), then wraps.
                    let z = 0.05 + 0.95 * (star.depth - time * speed).wrappedUnit
                    let zBehind = min(1, z + trail)
                    let head = CGPoint(x: centre.x + star.x / z * scale * 0.15, y: centre.y + star.y / z * scale * 0.15)
                    let tail = CGPoint(x: centre.x + star.x / zBehind * scale * 0.15, y: centre.y + star.y / zBehind * scale * 0.15)
                    let brightness = min(1, (1 - z) * 1.4)
                    var streak = Path()
                    streak.move(to: tail)
                    streak.addLine(to: head)
                    context.stroke(
                        streak,
                        with: .color(color.opacity(brightness)),
                        style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: max(0.6, (1 - z) * 2.4), lineCap: .round)
                    )
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private struct Star {
        var x: Double
        var y: Double
        var depth: Double
    }
}

private extension Double {
    /// Wraps the value into 0..<1.
    var wrappedUnit: Double {
        let r = truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1)
        return r < 0 ? r + 1 : r
    }
}

#Preview {
    Starfield()
        .background(.black)
        .frame(width: 320, height: 220)
}
```

## Cover Flow (`cover-flow`)

Side items turn away in 3D, shrink and dim; the centre faces you.

- API: `CoverFlow(items) { item in }`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/CoverFlow.swift

### Usage

```swift
CoverFlow(albums) { album in
    Image(album.artwork)
        .resizable()
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12))
}
.frame(height: 220)
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI CoverFlow carousel (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with an optional selection binding, itemWidth (140), spacing (−10) and maxAngle (50°). Use a horizontal ScrollView + LazyHStack with .scrollTargetLayout(), .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), hidden indicators, .scrollPosition(id:anchor: .center) and contentMargins that centre the first and last items. In .visualEffect, read the item's frame in the .scrollView coordinate space, compute p = clamp((midX − viewport centre) / itemWidth, −1, 1) and apply rotation3DEffect of −p × maxAngle around the y axis (perspective 0.6), scale 1 − |p| × 0.18 and brightness −|p| × 0.25. Raise the selected item's zIndex. With Reduce Motion on, drop the rotation.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A horizontal carousel in the style of Cover Flow: the centred item faces
/// you, and items to either side turn away in 3D, recede and dim. Items snap
/// to the centre.
public struct CoverFlow<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Content: View>: View where Data.Element: Identifiable {
    private let items: Data
    private let selection: Binding<Data.Element.ID?>?
    private let itemWidth: CGFloat
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let maxAngle: Double
    private let content: (Data.Element) -> Content

    @State private var internalSelection: Data.Element.ID?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: One item per element.
    ///   - selection: Optional binding to the centred item; set it to scroll.
    ///   - itemWidth: Width of each item in points.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between items (negative values overlap them).
    ///   - maxAngle: How far side items turn, in degrees.
    ///   - content: Builds one item, usually artwork.
    public init(
        _ items: Data,
        selection: Binding<Data.Element.ID?>? = nil,
        itemWidth: CGFloat = 140,
        spacing: CGFloat = -10,
        maxAngle: Double = 50,
        @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Content
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.selection = selection
        self.itemWidth = itemWidth
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.maxAngle = maxAngle
        self.content = content
    }

    public var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            // Plain values for the visualEffect closure, which can't touch the view.
            let fallbackWidth = geometry.size.width
            let itemWidth = itemWidth
            let maxAngle = reduceMotion ? 0 : maxAngle
            ScrollView(.horizontal) {
                LazyHStack(spacing: spacing) {
                    ForEach(items) { item in
                        content(item)
                            .frame(width: itemWidth)
                            .visualEffect { view, proxy in
                                // -1 (one item left of centre) … 0 (centred) … 1.
                                let frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal))
                                let viewport = proxy.bounds(of: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal))?.width ?? fallbackWidth
                                let clamped = max(-1, min(1, (frame.midX - viewport / 2) / itemWidth))
                                let angle = -clamped * maxAngle
                                return view
                                    .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(angle), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0), perspective: 0.6)
                                    .scaleEffect(1 - abs(clamped) * 0.18)
                                    .brightness(-abs(clamped) * 0.25)
                            }
                            // Centred item draws on top of its neighbours.
                            .zIndex(isSelected(item) ? 1 : 0)
                            .id(item.id)
                    }
                }
                .scrollTargetLayout()
                .frame(height: geometry.size.height)
            }
            .contentMargins(.horizontal, max(0, (geometry.size.width - itemWidth) / 2), for: .scrollContent)
            .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)
            .scrollIndicators(.hidden)
            .scrollPosition(id: selection ?? $internalSelection, anchor: .center)
        }
    }

    private func isSelected(_ item: Data.Element) -> Bool {
        (selection?.wrappedValue ?? internalSelection) == item.id
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Album: Identifiable {
        let id: Int
        let color: Color
    }
    let albums = [Color.red, .orange, .yellow, .green, .teal, .blue, .indigo, .purple]
        .enumerated().map { Album(id: $0, color: $1) }
    return CoverFlow(albums) { album in
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
            .fill(album.color.gradient)
            .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
            .overlay(Image(systemName: "music.note").font(.largeTitle).foregroundStyle(.white))
    }
    .frame(height: 200)
}
```

## Float 3D (`float-3d`)

The view hovers: a gentle bob, a slow 3D sway and a breathing shadow.

- API: `.float3D()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Float3D.swift

### Usage

```swift
Image("product")
    .resizable()
    .scaledToFit()
    .frame(width: 180)
    .float3D()

BadgeView()
    .float3D(height: 6, angle: 8, period: 4, shadow: false)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .float3D(height:angle:period:shadow:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Inside TimelineView(.animation), let t = time × 2π / period (3 s) and lift = 0.5 + 0.5·sin t. Rotate the content in 3D by sin(t/2) × angle (12°) around the y axis and cos(0.7t) × angle/2 around the x axis (perspective 0.5), and move it up by height (10 pt) × lift. Behind it, at the bottom, draw a black ellipse 12 pt tall, 18 pt below, that gets lighter (opacity 0.25 − 0.1·lift), narrower (scale x 0.75 − 0.15·lift) and blurrier (6 + 4·lift) as the view rises. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Makes a view hover in space: it bobs up and down and slowly sways in 3D,
/// while its shadow shrinks and grows underneath. For hero images, product
/// shots, badges and empty-state illustrations.
struct Float3DModifier: ViewModifier {
    var height: CGFloat
    var angle: Double
    var period: Double
    var shadow: Bool

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let t = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * 2 * .pi / period
            // Bob: 0 at rest height, 1 at the top.
            let lift = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(t)
            content
                .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(sin(t * 0.5) * angle), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0), perspective: 0.5)
                .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(cos(t * 0.7) * angle * 0.5), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0), perspective: 0.5)
                .offset(y: -height * lift)
                .background(alignment: .bottom) {
                    if shadow {
                        Ellipse()
                            .fill(.black.opacity(0.25 - 0.1 * lift))
                            .frame(height: 12)
                            .scaleEffect(x: 0.75 - 0.15 * lift, y: 1)
                            .blur(radius: 6 + 4 * lift)
                            .offset(y: 18)
                    }
                }
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Floats the view in 3D: a gentle bob, a slow sway and a breathing shadow.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("product")
    ///     .resizable()
    ///     .scaledToFit()
    ///     .frame(width: 180)
    ///     .float3D()
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - height: How high the view rises, in points.
    ///   - angle: Maximum sway angle, in degrees.
    ///   - period: Seconds for one bob up and down.
    ///   - shadow: Draws a soft ground shadow under the view.
    func float3D(height: CGFloat = 10, angle: Double = 12, period: Double = 3, shadow: Bool = true) -> some View {
        modifier(Float3DModifier(height: height, angle: angle, period: period, shadow: shadow))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 24, style: .continuous)
        .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [.cyan, .blue], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
        .frame(width: 140, height: 140)
        .overlay(Image(systemName: "cube.fill").font(.system(size: 56)).foregroundStyle(.white))
        .float3D()
        .padding(60)
}
```

## Fireworks (`fireworks`)

Rockets climb and burst into rings of falling, fading sparks.

- API: `Fireworks()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Fireworks.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack {
    Color.black.ignoresSafeArea()
    Fireworks()
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    Text("Happy New Year").font(.largeTitle.bold())
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Fireworks view (iOS 17+) with colors, interval (0.9 s between launches) and sparks (36 per burst), drawn statelessly in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Rocket k launches at k × interval; for every rocket younger than 0.8 s climb + 1.5 s fade, seed a SplitMix64 generator with k to pick x (15–85 % of the width), peak height (15–45 %), colour and reach (22–34 % of the smaller side). Climbing: ease-out from the bottom to the peak and draw a 14 pt trail. Bursting, with t = time since the burst / 1.5: place each spark at angle i / sparks × 2π (plus jitter), distance reach × (1 − (1 − min(1, 1.6 t))³) × random 0.75–1, add gravity fall t² × 0.6 × reach, draw a circle of radius 1.8 × (1 − 0.6 t) at opacity 1 − t, and add a white flash for the first 15 %. Hide from accessibility; with Reduce Motion on, freeze on a frame with a burst in bloom.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Rockets climb from the bottom of the view and burst into rings of falling,
/// fading sparks, one after another.
public struct Fireworks: View {
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let interval: Double
    private let sparks: Int

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - colors: Burst colours, picked per rocket.
    ///   - interval: Seconds between launches.
    ///   - sparks: Sparks per burst.
    public init(
        colors: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .yellow, .mint, .cyan, .purple],
        interval: Double = 0.9,
        sparks: Int = 36
    ) {
        self.colors = colors.isEmpty ? [.white] : colors
        self.interval = max(0.2, interval)
        self.sparks = max(1, sparks)
    }

    /// Seconds from launch to burst, and from burst to fully faded.
    private static let climb = 0.8
    private static let fade = 1.5

    public var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: a still frame with a burst in full bloom.
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 1.3 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            Canvas { context, size in
                let lifetime = Self.climb + Self.fade
                let newest = Int((time / interval).rounded(.down))
                let oldest = newest - Int((lifetime / interval).rounded(.up))
                for rocket in max(0, oldest)...max(0, newest) {
                    let age = time - Double(rocket) * interval
                    guard age >= 0, age < lifetime else { continue }
                    draw(rocket: rocket, age: age, in: &context, size: size)
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func draw(rocket: Int, age: Double, in context: inout GraphicsContext, size: CGSize) {
        var random = SplitMix64(seed: UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: rocket) &* 2_654_435_761)
        let x = size.width * CGFloat(0.15 + 0.7 * random.unit())
        let peak = size.height * CGFloat(0.15 + 0.3 * random.unit())
        let color = colors[Int(random.unit() * Double(colors.count)) % colors.count]
        let reach = min(size.width, size.height) * CGFloat(0.22 + 0.12 * random.unit())

        if age < Self.climb {
            // Climbing: ease out toward the peak, with a short trail.
            let t = age / Self.climb
            let eased = 1 - pow(1 - t, 2)
            let y = size.height - (size.height - peak) * CGFloat(eased)
            var trail = Path()
            trail.move(to: CGPoint(x: x, y: y + 14))
            trail.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: x, y: y))
            context.stroke(trail, with: .color(color.opacity(0.8)), style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 2, lineCap: .round))
            return
        }

        // Burst: sparks fly out, slow down, fall under gravity and fade.
        let t = (age - Self.climb) / Self.fade
        let spread = CGFloat(1 - pow(1 - min(1, t * 1.6), 3))
        let fall = CGFloat(t * t) * reach * 0.6
        let opacity = max(0, 1 - t)
        for spark in 0..<sparks {
            let angle = Double(spark) / Double(sparks) * 2 * .pi + random.unit() * 0.1
            let distance = reach * spread * CGFloat(0.75 + 0.25 * random.unit())
            let point = CGPoint(x: x + CGFloat(cos(angle)) * distance, y: peak + CGFloat(sin(angle)) * distance + fall)
            let r = CGFloat(1.8 * (1 - t * 0.6))
            context.fill(
                Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: point.x - r, y: point.y - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2)),
                with: .color(color.opacity(opacity))
            )
        }
        // A flash at the moment of the burst.
        if t < 0.15 {
            let r = reach * 0.35 * CGFloat(t / 0.15)
            context.fill(
                Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: x - r, y: peak - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2)),
                with: .color(.white.opacity(0.5 * (1 - t / 0.15)))
            )
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    Fireworks()
        .background(Color(red: 0.03, green: 0.03, blue: 0.1))
        .frame(width: 320, height: 220)
}
```

## Snowfall & Rain (`snowfall`)

Drifting, swaying snowflakes or fast slanted rain, with depth.

- API: `Snowfall(.snow / .rain)`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Snowfall.swift

### Usage

```swift
Snowfall()
    .background(.indigo)
    .ignoresSafeArea()

Snowfall(.rain, count: 150, color: .white.opacity(0.8))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Snowfall view (iOS 17+) with a style (.snow or .rain), count (80), color and speed. Give each particle seeded random traits: start x and y (0–1), depth (0–1) and phase. In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), compute positions as pure functions of time, wrapped around the view so nothing is stored. Snow: fall speed 18 + 30 × depth pt/s, horizontal sway sin(time × (0.8 + depth) + phase) × (6 + 10 × depth) plus a slow 4 pt/s drift, radius 1 + 2.4 × depth, opacity 0.35 + 0.6 × depth, so small flakes look far away. Rain: fall speed 380 + 320 × depth, a streak 8 + 14 × depth long slanted by 0.25, width 0.8 + 0.8 × depth, opacity 0.25 + 0.5 × depth. Hide from accessibility; Reduce Motion pauses it.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Falling weather: snowflakes that drift and sway, or slanted streaks of rain.
public struct Snowfall: View {
    /// What falls.
    public enum Style: Sendable {
        /// Soft round flakes that sway side to side.
        case snow
        /// Fast, thin, slanted streaks.
        case rain
    }

    private let style: Style
    private let color: Color
    private let speed: Double
    private let seeds: [FallSeed]

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - style: `.snow` or `.rain`.
    ///   - count: Number of flakes or drops.
    ///   - color: Flake or drop colour.
    ///   - speed: 1 = default pace.
    public init(_ style: Style = .snow, count: Int = 80, color: Color = .white, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.style = style
        self.color = color
        self.speed = speed
        var generator = SplitMix64(seed: style == .snow ? 11 : 23)
        seeds = (0..<max(0, count)).map { _ in FallSeed(using: &generator) }
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            Canvas { context, size in
                for seed in seeds {
                    switch style {
                    case .snow: drawFlake(seed, time: time, in: &context, size: size)
                    case .rain: drawDrop(seed, time: time, in: &context, size: size)
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func drawFlake(_ seed: FallSeed, time: Double, in context: inout GraphicsContext, size: CGSize) {
        // Small flakes are "far away": slower and fainter, for depth.
        let fallSpeed = 18 + 30 * seed.depth
        let travel = size.height + 20
        let y = (seed.start.y * travel + CGFloat(time * fallSpeed)).wrapped(to: travel) - 10
        let sway = CGFloat(sin(time * (0.8 + seed.depth) + seed.phase)) * (6 + 10 * seed.depth)
        let x = (seed.start.x * size.width + sway + CGFloat(time * 4)).wrapped(to: size.width)
        let r = 1 + 2.4 * seed.depth
        context.fill(
            Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: x - r, y: y - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2)),
            with: .color(color.opacity(0.35 + 0.6 * seed.depth))
        )
    }

    private func drawDrop(_ seed: FallSeed, time: Double, in context: inout GraphicsContext, size: CGSize) {
        let fallSpeed = 380 + 320 * seed.depth
        let length = 8 + 14 * seed.depth
        let slant: CGFloat = 0.25
        let travel = size.height + length + 20
        let y = (seed.start.y * travel + CGFloat(time * fallSpeed)).wrapped(to: travel) - length
        let x = (seed.start.x * (size.width + 40) + y * slant).wrapped(to: size.width + 40) - 20
        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: x, y: y))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: x + length * slant, y: y + length))
        context.stroke(path, with: .color(color.opacity(0.25 + 0.5 * seed.depth)), style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 0.8 + 0.8 * seed.depth, lineCap: .round))
    }
}

/// Fixed random traits of one flake or drop.
private struct FallSeed {
    var start: CGPoint
    var depth: CGFloat
    var phase: Double

    init(using generator: inout SplitMix64) {
        start = CGPoint(x: generator.unit(), y: generator.unit())
        depth = CGFloat(generator.unit())
        phase = generator.unit() * 2 * .pi
    }
}

#Preview {
    HStack(spacing: 0) {
        Snowfall().background(Color(red: 0.1, green: 0.15, blue: 0.3))
        Snowfall(.rain, count: 120).background(Color(white: 0.15))
    }
    .frame(width: 320, height: 200)
}
```

## Floating Reactions (`floating-reactions`)

Live-stream style emoji float up, swaying, every time you react.

- API: `.floatingReactions(trigger:)`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/FloatingReactions.swift

### Usage

```swift
LiveVideo()
    .floatingReactions(trigger: reactionCount)

Button("❤️") { reactionCount += 1 }
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .floatingReactions(trigger:emojis:height:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Every time trigger changes, append a reaction (UUID, a random emoji from the list, a random sway of ±8–18 pt and drift of ±20 pt) to a @State array and remove it 2.3 s later. In a bottom-aligned, hit-testing-disabled overlay, show each emoji (28 pt) with keyframeAnimator(initialValue:trigger:), triggered by a @State flag set in onAppear so it plays once, over {y, x, scale, opacity}: y goes to −height (160 pt) over 2.2 s; x weaves sway → −sway + drift → sway + drift → drift in four 0.55 s cubic keyframes; scale springs from 0.3 to 1.15 and settles at 1; opacity holds for 1.4 s then fades over 0.8 s. With Reduce Motion on, don't spawn reactions.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Live-stream style reactions: every time `trigger` changes, an emoji pops
/// up from the bottom of the view, floats upward swaying, and fades out.
struct FloatingReactionsModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Trigger
    var emojis: [String]
    var height: CGFloat

    @State private var reactions: [FloatingReaction] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
                ZStack {
                    ForEach(reactions) { reaction in
                        FloatingEmoji(reaction: reaction, height: height)
                    }
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .onChange(of: trigger) {
                // Reduce Motion: no floating emoji.
                guard !reduceMotion, let emoji = emojis.randomElement() else { return }
                let reaction = FloatingReaction(
                    emoji: emoji,
                    sway: .random(in: 8...18) * (Bool.random() ? 1 : -1),
                    drift: .random(in: -20...20)
                )
                reactions.append(reaction)
                DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 2.3) {
                    reactions.removeAll { $0.id == reaction.id }
                }
            }
    }
}

/// One emoji on its way up, with its own random sway.
struct FloatingReaction: Identifiable {
    let id = UUID()
    let emoji: String
    let sway: CGFloat
    let drift: CGFloat
}

private struct FloatValues {
    var y: CGFloat = 0
    var x: CGFloat = 0
    var scale: CGFloat = 0.3
    var opacity: Double = 1
}

private struct FloatingEmoji: View {
    let reaction: FloatingReaction
    let height: CGFloat

    /// Flipped on appear to play the keyframes once (the `repeating: false`
    /// variant never plays them at all).
    @State private var launched = false

    var body: some View {
        let sway = reaction.sway
        let drift = reaction.drift
        let height = height
        Text(reaction.emoji)
            .font(.system(size: 28))
            .onAppear { launched = true }
            .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: FloatValues(), trigger: launched) { view, value in
                view
                    .scaleEffect(value.scale)
                    .offset(x: value.x, y: value.y)
                    .opacity(value.opacity)
            } keyframes: { _ in
                KeyframeTrack(\.y) {
                    CubicKeyframe(-height, duration: 2.2)
                }
                KeyframeTrack(\.x) {
                    CubicKeyframe(sway, duration: 0.55)
                    CubicKeyframe(-sway + drift, duration: 0.55)
                    CubicKeyframe(sway + drift, duration: 0.55)
                    CubicKeyframe(drift, duration: 0.55)
                }
                KeyframeTrack(\.scale) {
                    SpringKeyframe(1.15, duration: 0.25, spring: .bouncy)
                    CubicKeyframe(1, duration: 0.3)
                }
                KeyframeTrack(\.opacity) {
                    LinearKeyframe(1, duration: 1.4)
                    LinearKeyframe(0, duration: 0.8)
                }
            }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Floats an emoji up from the bottom of the view every time `trigger`
    /// changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// LiveVideo()
    ///     .floatingReactions(trigger: reactionCount)
    ///
    /// Button("❤️") { reactionCount += 1 }
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - emojis: One is picked at random for each reaction.
    ///   - height: How far each reaction rises, in points.
    func floatingReactions<Trigger: Equatable>(
        trigger: Trigger,
        emojis: [String] = ["❤️", "🔥", "👏", "😂", "😍"],
        height: CGFloat = 160
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(FloatingReactionsModifier(trigger: trigger, emojis: emojis, height: height))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var count = 0
        var body: some View {
            Button("React") { count += 1 }
                .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                .floatingReactions(trigger: count)
                .padding(.top, 180)
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}
```

## Warp Tunnel (`warp-tunnel`)

Rings rush out of the vanishing point toward you: flying down a tunnel.

- API: `WarpTunnel()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/WarpTunnel.swift

### Usage

```swift
WarpTunnel()
    .background(.black)
    .ignoresSafeArea()

WarpTunnel(colors: [.green, .mint], sides: 6) // hexagons
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI WarpTunnel view (iOS 17+) with rings (18), colors (cyan, blue, purple, pink), speed (1.2 rings per second) and sides (0 for circles, 3+ for polygons). In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), for ring i let depth = 1 − (i + fract(time × speed)) / rings and skip depths below 0.02. Its radius is half the view's diagonal × 0.06 / depth (perspective), skipped once it's 1.5 × larger than that. Stroke a circle, or a polygon rotated by i × 0.12 + time × 0.1 rad, centred in the view, with opacity closeness² and line width 0.5 + 3 × closeness (closeness = 1 − depth), cycling colours by ring. Hide from accessibility; Reduce Motion pauses it.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Flying through a tunnel: rings rush out of the vanishing point toward the
/// viewer, growing, brightening and turning as they pass.
public struct WarpTunnel: View {
    private let rings: Int
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let speed: Double
    private let sides: Int

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - rings: Number of rings in the tunnel.
    ///   - colors: Ring colours, cycled from the back of the tunnel.
    ///   - speed: Rings passed per second.
    ///   - sides: 0 for circles, 3 or more for polygons (6 = hexagons).
    public init(
        rings: Int = 18,
        colors: [Color] = [.cyan, .blue, .purple, .pink],
        speed: Double = 1.2,
        sides: Int = 0
    ) {
        self.rings = max(2, rings)
        self.colors = colors.isEmpty ? [.white] : colors
        self.speed = speed
        self.sides = sides
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            Canvas { context, size in
                let centre = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
                let reach = hypot(size.width, size.height) / 2
                let offset = time - time.rounded(.down)
                for ring in 0..<rings {
                    // Depth 1 is the far end, near 0 the viewer.
                    let depth = 1 - (Double(ring) + offset) / Double(rings)
                    guard depth > 0.02 else { continue }
                    let radius = reach * CGFloat(0.06 / depth)
                    guard radius < reach * 1.5 else { continue }
                    let closeness = 1 - depth
                    let index = (Int(time.rounded(.down)) + ring) % colors.count
                    let path = ringPath(centre: centre, radius: radius, rotation: Double(ring) * 0.12 + time * 0.1)
                    context.stroke(
                        path,
                        with: .color(colors[index].opacity(closeness * closeness)),
                        lineWidth: 0.5 + 3 * CGFloat(closeness)
                    )
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func ringPath(centre: CGPoint, radius: CGFloat, rotation: Double) -> Path {
        guard sides >= 3 else {
            return Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: centre.x - radius, y: centre.y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2))
        }
        var path = Path()
        for corner in 0...sides {
            let angle = Double(corner) / Double(sides) * 2 * .pi + rotation
            let point = CGPoint(x: centre.x + CGFloat(cos(angle)) * radius, y: centre.y + CGFloat(sin(angle)) * radius)
            corner == 0 ? path.move(to: point) : path.addLine(to: point)
        }
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

#Preview {
    WarpTunnel(sides: 6)
        .background(.black)
        .frame(width: 320, height: 220)
}
```

## Holographic Card (`holo-card`)

A trading card that tilts toward you with a rainbow foil and moving glare.

- API: `.holographic()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Hover / Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Holographic.swift

### Usage

```swift
Image("card-art")
    .resizable()
    .aspectRatio(5 / 7, contentMode: .fit)
    .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16))
    .holographic(cornerRadius: 16)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .holographic(cornerRadius:maxAngle:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Track the pointer with .onContinuousHover and a finger with a simultaneous DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0), normalising the location to p in −1…1 on both axes (nil when released). Overlay, clipped to a continuous rounded rectangle: (1) a rainbow LinearGradient (red → … → purple → red) from (−0.5 + 0.6 px, −0.5 + 0.3 py) to (1.5 + 0.6 px, 1.5 + 0.3 py) with .blendMode(.overlay), at 55 % opacity while touched and 15 % at rest; (2) a white 70 % → clear RadialGradient centred at (0.5 + 0.5 px, 0.5 + 0.5 py) with .blendMode(.softLight), visible only while touched. Tilt with rotation3DEffect: −py × maxAngle (14°) around x and px × maxAngle around y, perspective 0.6, and scale to 1.03 while touched. Follow with .interactiveSpring(response: 0.25) and release with .spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.6). With Reduce Motion on, keep the foil and glare but don't tilt or scale.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A collectible-card shine: the view tilts toward the pointer or finger, a
/// rainbow foil slides across it and a white glare follows the light source.
/// Springs back flat on release.
struct HolographicModifier: ViewModifier {
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat
    var maxAngle: Double

    /// Pointer position in -1…1 on both axes; nil when not touching.
    @State private var pointer: CGPoint?
    @State private var size: CGSize = .zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let p = pointer ?? .zero
        let active = pointer != nil
        let shape = RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous)
        content
            .overlay {
                ZStack {
                    // Rainbow foil, shifted by the tilt.
                    LinearGradient(
                        colors: [.red, .orange, .yellow, .green, .cyan, .blue, .purple, .red],
                        startPoint: UnitPoint(x: -0.5 + p.x * 0.6, y: -0.5 + p.y * 0.3),
                        endPoint: UnitPoint(x: 1.5 + p.x * 0.6, y: 1.5 + p.y * 0.3)
                    )
                    .blendMode(.overlay)
                    .opacity(active ? 0.55 : 0.15)

                    // Glare where the light hits.
                    RadialGradient(
                        colors: [.white.opacity(0.7), .white.opacity(0)],
                        center: UnitPoint(x: 0.5 + p.x * 0.5, y: 0.5 + p.y * 0.5),
                        startRadius: 0,
                        endRadius: max(size.width, size.height) * 0.6
                    )
                    .blendMode(.softLight)
                    .opacity(active ? 1 : 0)
                }
                .clipShape(shape)
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .background {
                GeometryReader { geometry in
                    Color.clear
                        .onAppear { size = geometry.size }
                        .onChange(of: geometry.size) { _, newSize in size = newSize }
                }
            }
            // Reduce Motion: the foil and glare still react, but the card stays flat.
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(reduceMotion ? 0 : Double(p.y) * -maxAngle), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0), perspective: 0.6)
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(reduceMotion ? 0 : Double(p.x) * maxAngle), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0), perspective: 0.6)
            .scaleEffect(active && !reduceMotion ? 1.03 : 1)
            .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) { phase in
                switch phase {
                case let .active(location): track(location)
                case .ended: release()
                }
            }
            .simultaneousGesture(
                DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0, coordinateSpace: .local)
                    .onChanged { track($0.location) }
                    .onEnded { _ in release() }
            )
    }

    private func track(_ location: CGPoint) {
        guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0 else { return }
        let x = min(1, max(-1, location.x / size.width * 2 - 1))
        let y = min(1, max(-1, location.y / size.height * 2 - 1))
        withAnimation(.interactiveSpring(response: 0.25, dampingFraction: 0.8)) {
            pointer = CGPoint(x: x, y: y)
        }
    }

    private func release() {
        withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.6)) { pointer = nil }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Turns the view into a holographic trading card that tilts and shines
    /// under the pointer or finger.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("card-art")
    ///     .resizable()
    ///     .aspectRatio(5 / 7, contentMode: .fit)
    ///     .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16))
    ///     .holographic(cornerRadius: 16)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - cornerRadius: Match the view's own corner radius.
    ///   - maxAngle: Tilt at the edges, in degrees.
    func holographic(cornerRadius: CGFloat = 16, maxAngle: Double = 14) -> some View {
        modifier(HolographicModifier(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, maxAngle: maxAngle))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16, style: .continuous)
        .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
        .overlay(Image(systemName: "bolt.fill").font(.system(size: 50)).foregroundStyle(.yellow))
        .frame(width: 150, height: 210)
        .holographic()
        .padding(40)
}
```

## Iris (`iris`)

A circle opens from a point to reveal the view, like a camera iris.

- API: `.transition(.iris)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift

### Usage

```swift
if showPhoto {
    PhotoView()
        .transition(.iris)
}

DetailView()
    .transition(.iris(origin: .topTrailing))
```

### How it works

Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+, the Transition protocol) called IrisTransition with an origin UnitPoint (centre), exposed as .iris and .iris(origin:). In body(content:phase:), mask the content with a GeometryReader containing a Circle whose radius is the distance from the origin point to the furthest corner, positioned at the origin, with scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: origin). The circle grows from the origin to cover the view on insertion and closes back on removal, timed by whatever animation drives the change, e.g. withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.6)). It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Transitions that reveal or hide a view through an animated mask. Masks
// don't move the content, so they need no Reduce Motion fallback.

// MARK: - Iris

/// A circle that opens from a point to reveal the view, and closes back to
/// it on removal, like a camera iris.
public struct IrisTransition: Transition {
    public var origin: UnitPoint

    public init(origin: UnitPoint = .center) {
        self.origin = origin
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                let size = geometry.size
                let o = CGPoint(x: size.width * origin.x, y: size.height * origin.y)
                // Far enough to cover the corner furthest from the origin.
                let radius = [CGPoint.zero, CGPoint(x: size.width, y: 0), CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height), CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height)]
                    .map { hypot($0.x - o.x, $0.y - o.y) }
                    .max() ?? 0
                Circle()
                    .frame(width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)
                    .position(o)
                    .scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: origin)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == IrisTransition {
    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from its centre.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showPhoto {
    ///     PhotoView().transition(.iris)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var iris: IrisTransition { IrisTransition() }

    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from `origin`.
    static func iris(origin: UnitPoint) -> IrisTransition { IrisTransition(origin: origin) }
}

// MARK: - Blinds

/// Horizontal slats that open together, like Venetian blinds.
public struct BlindsTransition: Transition {
    public var slats: Int

    public init(slats: Int = 8) {
        self.slats = max(1, slats)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                ForEach(0..<slats, id: \.self) { _ in
                    Rectangle()
                        .scaleEffect(y: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: .top)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == BlindsTransition {
    /// Reveals the view through opening blinds.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Banner().transition(.blinds)
    /// ```
    static var blinds: BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition() }

    /// Reveals the view through `slats` opening blinds.
    static func blinds(slats: Int) -> BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition(slats: slats) }
}

// MARK: - Clock wipe

/// A wedge that sweeps clockwise from twelve o'clock, like a clock hand.
public struct ClockWipeTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            ClockWipeShape(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
        }
    }
}

struct ClockWipeShape: Shape {
    var progress: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        guard progress < 1 else { return Path(rect) }
        guard progress > 0 else { return Path() }
        let centre = CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
        let radius = hypot(rect.width, rect.height)
        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: centre)
        // In SwiftUI's y-down space, clockwise: false sweeps clockwise on screen.
        path.addArc(center: centre, radius: radius, startAngle: .degrees(-90), endAngle: .degrees(-90 + 360 * progress), clockwise: false)
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == ClockWipeTransition {
    /// Sweeps the view in like the hand of a clock.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Badge().transition(.clockWipe)
    /// ```
    static var clockWipe: ClockWipeTransition { ClockWipeTransition() }
}

// MARK: - Dissolve

/// The view appears and disappears in square pixels, in random order.
public struct DissolveTransition: Transition {
    public var cellSize: CGFloat

    public init(cellSize: CGFloat = 10) {
        self.cellSize = max(2, cellSize)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            DissolveShape(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0, cellSize: cellSize)
        }
    }
}

struct DissolveShape: Shape {
    var progress: Double
    var cellSize: CGFloat

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        guard progress < 1 else { return Path(rect) }
        var path = Path()
        guard progress > 0 else { return path }
        let columns = Int((rect.width / cellSize).rounded(.up))
        let rows = Int((rect.height / cellSize).rounded(.up))
        for row in 0..<rows {
            for column in 0..<columns where Self.threshold(column, row) < progress {
                // A hair larger than the cell so neighbours don't leave seams.
                path.addRect(CGRect(x: rect.minX + CGFloat(column) * cellSize, y: rect.minY + CGFloat(row) * cellSize, width: cellSize, height: cellSize).insetBy(dx: -0.25, dy: -0.25))
            }
        }
        return path
    }

    /// A stable pseudo-random value in 0..<1 for each cell.
    static func threshold(_ column: Int, _ row: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: column &* 73_856_093 ^ row &* 19_349_663)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd
        x ^= x >> 33
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == DissolveTransition {
    /// Dissolves the view in and out in random square pixels.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Avatar().transition(.dissolve)
    /// ```
    static var dissolve: DissolveTransition { DissolveTransition() }

    /// Dissolves the view in and out in random pixels of `cellSize` points.
    static func dissolve(cellSize: CGFloat) -> DissolveTransition { DissolveTransition(cellSize: cellSize) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shown = true
        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                HStack(spacing: 12) {
                    ForEach(0..<4, id: \.self) { index in
                        ZStack {
                            if shown {
                                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
                                    .fill(Color.blue.gradient)
                                    .transition(index == 0 ? AnyTransition(.iris) : index == 1 ? AnyTransition(.blinds) : index == 2 ? AnyTransition(.clockWipe) : AnyTransition(.dissolve))
                            }
                        }
                        .frame(width: 64, height: 64)
                    }
                }
                Button("Toggle") { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8)) { shown.toggle() } }
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}
```

## Blinds (`blinds`)

Horizontal slats open together to reveal the view, like Venetian blinds.

- API: `.transition(.blinds)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift

### Usage

```swift
Banner()
    .transition(.blinds)

Poster()
    .transition(.blinds(slats: 12))
```

### How it works

Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called BlindsTransition with a slats count (8), exposed as .blinds and .blinds(slats:). In body(content:phase:), mask the content with a VStack(spacing: 0) of slats Rectangles, each with scaleEffect(y: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: .top), so every slat grows down from its top edge at the same time on insertion and folds back up on removal. It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Transitions that reveal or hide a view through an animated mask. Masks
// don't move the content, so they need no Reduce Motion fallback.

// MARK: - Iris

/// A circle that opens from a point to reveal the view, and closes back to
/// it on removal, like a camera iris.
public struct IrisTransition: Transition {
    public var origin: UnitPoint

    public init(origin: UnitPoint = .center) {
        self.origin = origin
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                let size = geometry.size
                let o = CGPoint(x: size.width * origin.x, y: size.height * origin.y)
                // Far enough to cover the corner furthest from the origin.
                let radius = [CGPoint.zero, CGPoint(x: size.width, y: 0), CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height), CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height)]
                    .map { hypot($0.x - o.x, $0.y - o.y) }
                    .max() ?? 0
                Circle()
                    .frame(width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)
                    .position(o)
                    .scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: origin)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == IrisTransition {
    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from its centre.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showPhoto {
    ///     PhotoView().transition(.iris)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var iris: IrisTransition { IrisTransition() }

    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from `origin`.
    static func iris(origin: UnitPoint) -> IrisTransition { IrisTransition(origin: origin) }
}

// MARK: - Blinds

/// Horizontal slats that open together, like Venetian blinds.
public struct BlindsTransition: Transition {
    public var slats: Int

    public init(slats: Int = 8) {
        self.slats = max(1, slats)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                ForEach(0..<slats, id: \.self) { _ in
                    Rectangle()
                        .scaleEffect(y: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: .top)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == BlindsTransition {
    /// Reveals the view through opening blinds.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Banner().transition(.blinds)
    /// ```
    static var blinds: BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition() }

    /// Reveals the view through `slats` opening blinds.
    static func blinds(slats: Int) -> BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition(slats: slats) }
}

// MARK: - Clock wipe

/// A wedge that sweeps clockwise from twelve o'clock, like a clock hand.
public struct ClockWipeTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            ClockWipeShape(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
        }
    }
}

struct ClockWipeShape: Shape {
    var progress: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        guard progress < 1 else { return Path(rect) }
        guard progress > 0 else { return Path() }
        let centre = CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
        let radius = hypot(rect.width, rect.height)
        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: centre)
        // In SwiftUI's y-down space, clockwise: false sweeps clockwise on screen.
        path.addArc(center: centre, radius: radius, startAngle: .degrees(-90), endAngle: .degrees(-90 + 360 * progress), clockwise: false)
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == ClockWipeTransition {
    /// Sweeps the view in like the hand of a clock.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Badge().transition(.clockWipe)
    /// ```
    static var clockWipe: ClockWipeTransition { ClockWipeTransition() }
}

// MARK: - Dissolve

/// The view appears and disappears in square pixels, in random order.
public struct DissolveTransition: Transition {
    public var cellSize: CGFloat

    public init(cellSize: CGFloat = 10) {
        self.cellSize = max(2, cellSize)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            DissolveShape(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0, cellSize: cellSize)
        }
    }
}

struct DissolveShape: Shape {
    var progress: Double
    var cellSize: CGFloat

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        guard progress < 1 else { return Path(rect) }
        var path = Path()
        guard progress > 0 else { return path }
        let columns = Int((rect.width / cellSize).rounded(.up))
        let rows = Int((rect.height / cellSize).rounded(.up))
        for row in 0..<rows {
            for column in 0..<columns where Self.threshold(column, row) < progress {
                // A hair larger than the cell so neighbours don't leave seams.
                path.addRect(CGRect(x: rect.minX + CGFloat(column) * cellSize, y: rect.minY + CGFloat(row) * cellSize, width: cellSize, height: cellSize).insetBy(dx: -0.25, dy: -0.25))
            }
        }
        return path
    }

    /// A stable pseudo-random value in 0..<1 for each cell.
    static func threshold(_ column: Int, _ row: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: column &* 73_856_093 ^ row &* 19_349_663)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd
        x ^= x >> 33
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == DissolveTransition {
    /// Dissolves the view in and out in random square pixels.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Avatar().transition(.dissolve)
    /// ```
    static var dissolve: DissolveTransition { DissolveTransition() }

    /// Dissolves the view in and out in random pixels of `cellSize` points.
    static func dissolve(cellSize: CGFloat) -> DissolveTransition { DissolveTransition(cellSize: cellSize) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shown = true
        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                HStack(spacing: 12) {
                    ForEach(0..<4, id: \.self) { index in
                        ZStack {
                            if shown {
                                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
                                    .fill(Color.blue.gradient)
                                    .transition(index == 0 ? AnyTransition(.iris) : index == 1 ? AnyTransition(.blinds) : index == 2 ? AnyTransition(.clockWipe) : AnyTransition(.dissolve))
                            }
                        }
                        .frame(width: 64, height: 64)
                    }
                }
                Button("Toggle") { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8)) { shown.toggle() } }
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}
```

## Clock Wipe (`clock-wipe`)

A wedge sweeps clockwise from twelve o'clock, like a clock hand.

- API: `.transition(.clockWipe)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift

### Usage

```swift
Badge()
    .transition(.clockWipe)
```

### How it works

Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called ClockWipeTransition, exposed as .clockWipe. Mask the content with an animatable Shape whose animatableData is progress (0…1): it returns the full rect at 1, an empty path at 0, and otherwise a pie wedge from the centre with radius equal to the rect's diagonal, from −90° to −90° + 360° × progress (clockwise: false, which sweeps clockwise on screen in SwiftUI's y-down space). Pass progress 1 when phase.isIdentity and 0 otherwise, so the animation interpolates the angle. It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Transitions that reveal or hide a view through an animated mask. Masks
// don't move the content, so they need no Reduce Motion fallback.

// MARK: - Iris

/// A circle that opens from a point to reveal the view, and closes back to
/// it on removal, like a camera iris.
public struct IrisTransition: Transition {
    public var origin: UnitPoint

    public init(origin: UnitPoint = .center) {
        self.origin = origin
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                let size = geometry.size
                let o = CGPoint(x: size.width * origin.x, y: size.height * origin.y)
                // Far enough to cover the corner furthest from the origin.
                let radius = [CGPoint.zero, CGPoint(x: size.width, y: 0), CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height), CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height)]
                    .map { hypot($0.x - o.x, $0.y - o.y) }
                    .max() ?? 0
                Circle()
                    .frame(width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)
                    .position(o)
                    .scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: origin)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == IrisTransition {
    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from its centre.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showPhoto {
    ///     PhotoView().transition(.iris)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var iris: IrisTransition { IrisTransition() }

    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from `origin`.
    static func iris(origin: UnitPoint) -> IrisTransition { IrisTransition(origin: origin) }
}

// MARK: - Blinds

/// Horizontal slats that open together, like Venetian blinds.
public struct BlindsTransition: Transition {
    public var slats: Int

    public init(slats: Int = 8) {
        self.slats = max(1, slats)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {

                ForEach(0..<slats, id: \.self) { _ in
                    Rectangle()
                        .scaleEffect(y: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: .top)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

    /// Reveals the view through opening blinds.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Banner().transition(.blinds)
    /// ```
    static var blinds: BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition() }

    /// Reveals the view through `slats` opening blinds.
    static func blinds(slats: Int) -> BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition(slats: slats) }
}

## Pixel Dissolve (`dissolve`)

The view appears and vanishes in square pixels, in random order.

- API: `.transition(.dissolve)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift

### Usage

```swift
Avatar()
    .transition(.dissolve)

Artwork()
    .transition(.dissolve(cellSize: 6))
```

### How it works

Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called DissolveTransition with a cellSize (10 pt), exposed as .dissolve and .dissolve(cellSize:). Mask the content with an animatable Shape whose animatableData is progress (0…1): divide the rect into a grid of cellSize squares, give each cell a stable pseudo-random threshold in 0…1 from an integer hash of (column, row), and add the cells whose threshold is below progress (outset by 0.25 pt so neighbours don't leave seams); return the full rect at 1 and an empty path at 0. Pass progress 1 when phase.isIdentity and 0 otherwise. It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Transitions that reveal or hide a view through an animated mask. Masks
// don't move the content, so they need no Reduce Motion fallback.

// MARK: - Iris

/// A circle that opens from a point to reveal the view, and closes back to
/// it on removal, like a camera iris.
public struct IrisTransition: Transition {
    public var origin: UnitPoint

    public init(origin: UnitPoint = .center) {
        self.origin = origin
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                let size = geometry.size
                let o = CGPoint(x: size.width * origin.x, y: size.height * origin.y)
                // Far enough to cover the corner furthest from the origin.
                let radius = [CGPoint.zero, CGPoint(x: size.width, y: 0), CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height), CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height)]
                    .map { hypot($0.x - o.x, $0.y - o.y) }
                    .max() ?? 0
                Circle()
                    .frame(width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)
                    .position(o)
                    .scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: origin)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == IrisTransition {
    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from its centre.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showPhoto {
    ///     PhotoView().transition(.iris)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var iris: IrisTransition { IrisTransition() }

    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from `origin`.
    static func iris(origin: UnitPoint) -> IrisTransition { IrisTransition(origin: origin) }
}

// MARK: - Blinds

/// Horizontal slats that open together, like Venetian blinds.

    public var slats: Int

    public init(slats: Int = 8) {
        self.slats = max(1, slats)
    }

        content.mask {
            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                ForEach(0..<slats, id: \.self) { _ in

                        .scaleEffect(y: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: .top)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Banner().transition(.blinds)
    /// ```
